Settlement_Description: Used to be a Slavic settlement, a German castle was probably built around 1137, a German settlement developed around the church of St Nicholas.
Town_Description: Most likely founded around 1200 by the lords of the castle and the land, initiated by merchants of Salzwedel. First mentioned as town ('civitas') in 1239.
Harbour_Description: The Stepenitz was used as a waterway between Perleberg and the Elbe in Wittenberge, as is derived from the establishment of a Stepenitz toll on river transport in Wittenberge in 1337.

name: Liepupe
Settlement_Description: The settlement and manor were first mentioned in 1372. In 1490 an inn is mentioned. In 1544 a fortified borough ('Hakelwerk') was built.

name: Perow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1304.

name: Petersberg (Halle)
Settlement_Description: Around 1000 a chapel was built from which Slavs were attempted to be proselitysed. The chapel had its high time in the 11th and 12th century, after that it declined in meaning but remained a popular pilgrimage site.

name: Grimma
Settlement_Description: A Slavic fishing village before the 12th century, first mentioned in 1160; a German castle settlement is attested around 1330. A town was founded at the end of the 12th century.
Fair_Description: The regulations of safe conduct from 1390 also come with the privilege for two fairs.
Toll_Description: Toll station of the Margrave of Meißen. Toll and safe conduct regulations remain from 1390, 1524/25 and 1621.

name: Petershagen (Weser)
Settlement_Description: Near the settlement Huculvi / Hokelve, already mentioned in 784, the bishop of Minden built the castle Petershagen in 1306; the associated settlement acquired borough ('weichbild') privileges around 1360.
Toll_Description: Emperor Charles IV granted Petershagen toll privileges in 1377. The toll is mentioned in lists of Weser tolls in 1584 and 1597. A register of toll receipts is still extant for 1565/66 (Landesarchiv NRW, KDK Minden Nr. 2607).

name: Piotrków Trybunalski
Toll_Description: A toll station is mentioned in 1344. In 1390 King Władysław of Poland ordained, that the toll tariffs in Sieradz, Kalisz, Pyzdry and Poznań were to be the same as those levied in Piotrków Trybunalski, Łęczyca, Przedecz and Brześć.

name: Witten
Settlement_Description: Goes back to a Carolingian settlement, where a church village emerged. First mentioned in 1016.

name: Pöide
Settlement_Description: Village, which was situated around the chapel that was built in the middle of the 13th century.

name: Brody
Settlement_Description: The settlement probably developed as a borough near a castle ('Burgflecken'). The castle was probably located at the site of the later palace, but is not attested in written records. It was still a parish village in 1346.
Town_Description: No official founding date, it possessed town privileges since the second half of the 16th century. Usually called town or small town ('Städtlein').
Toll_Description: Görlitz complained in 1438 at the court of King Albrecht about the levying of a new toll in Pförten.

name: Pikknurme
Settlement_Description: In 1560 the mill and other parts of the village burned down.

name: Baltiysk
Settlement_Description: During the time of the Teutonic Order, fishing villages were mentioned, in 1413, 1476 and 1583. After storm surges had created direct access to the Baltic Sea between 1479 and 1510 the settlement became more important. A fortress was built in 1625 to protect the shipping lane, next to which a new town developed.
Harbour_Description: Pillau became an important harbour when storm surges created a gap in the Vistula spit near the settlement between 1479 and 1510 near the settlement, making it the sea harbour for the Vistula Lagoon.

name: Petschow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1327.

name: Piiumetsa
Settlement_Description: The manor and village were first mentioned in 1423. In 1593 there was also a mill.

name: Plaußig
Settlement_Description: Mentioned as manor in 1275; dince 1393 mentioned as knightly manor.

name: Pirna
Settlement_Description: There was a Slavic pre-settlement. In the 11./12th century a castle was built. Close to that, there were two fishermen's settlements and a market place since 1200, which was further expanded.
Town_Description: Margrave Heinrich III of Meißen granted Magdeburg town privileges between 1234 and 1245.
Toll_Description: The toll on the Elbe in Pirna is first mentioned in 1269 and was closely connected to the staple. The oldest known tariffs date from 1325, which also mention a land toll for salt wagons. The toll was regulated quite minutely, as well as the duties of the ferrymen. The fee registry mentions that whatever cannot be found listed, should be looked for in the list of Königsstein (Elbe). The registry differentiates between the safe conduct on the water and by land. Returning boats were exempt from the toll. The regulations of safe-conduct do not mention rafts, which leads to believe that traffic with large transport rafts only began from Pirna. It appears to be the starting point of trade down the Elbe river.
Staple_Description: Originally only a staple for salt and grain and a compulsory exchange of goods; later a general staple. The staple is first mentioned in 1291 upon sale of the town; confirmed in 1325. In 1520 and 1565 merchants from Dresden are partially excepted.

name: Pißdorf
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1344.
Toll_Description: Secondary station of safe conducht ('Beigeleitsstelle') of Köthen, mentioned in 1563.

name: Platenlaase
Settlement_Description: Originally called Lase, the addition Platen- (after the location near the settlement Plate) dates from modern times to discern the settlement from Laase. In 1450, the village consisted of 6 farms.

name: Kerkrade
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1108 or shortly after. Next mention in 1241.

name: Plau am See
Settlement_Description: Originally a Slavic settlement and fortification, which belonged to the Lords of Werle around 1200. First mentioned when a town was founded here in 1225.
Town_Description: The town was founded by Lord Heinrich Borwin I around 1225, Parchim town law granted before 1235.

name: Plaue (Havel)
Settlement_Description: First mention of Plaue in a record from 1198, probably founded soon after the Slavic uprising in 1147. Mention of the castrum Plaue in 1324.
Town_Description: A town foundation is unknown. Citizens are mentioned in 1385, the settlement is mentioned as town in 1411, but otherwise only as small town or borough ('Flecken').
Fair_Description: In 1559 a council scale and two fairs are granted to Plaue.
Toll_Description: Toll and safe conduct fees attested since 1334, when they were pawned off by the archbishop of Magdeburg. After 1575 the bridge toll is abolished and the maintenance of the bridge and dam had to be paid from the income of the regular horse- and walking fee ('Pferde- und Fußzoll'). A toll registry ('Geleitstafel') remains from 1626.

name: Plattenburg
Settlement_Description: First mention of the castle occurs in 1319 when it is sold to the bishop of Havelberg, but it was probably already constructed in the 13th century.

name: Płock
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station in c. 1349, where 3 gr. and 4 den. had to be paid for each horse.

name: Plön
Settlement_Description: Slavic fortification, built around 900, destroyed in 1139. Around 1156, the castle was rebuilt by count Adolf II of Holstein. Around the same time, a market and church settlement came into being.
Town_Description: Lübeck town privileges granted by Count Adolf IV in 1236.
Fair_Description: Heinrich Rantzau mentions in his 1597 description of Schleswig and Holstein a fair 14 days after St Michael's Day.

name: Plötzkau
Settlement_Description: First mention of a count of Plötzkau in 1069. The castle changed ownership several times until the 19th century.

name: Pogeez
Toll_Description: In 1424, it is mentioned that a toll was levied on timber cargoes in Pogeez. It is unknown whether the toll was levied on other commodities as well.

name: Pölbitz
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1219. It became part of Zwickau in 1895.

name: Pölchow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1275.

name: Policko
Toll_Description: A toll at the crossing of the Obra in Policko is first mentioned in the 13th century and still attested in the 16th.

name: Polatsk
Staple_Description: Grand Duke Witold attempted to turn Polozk into a trading centre between Riga and Smolensk. In 1406 the town aquired the right to trade beyond Riga and to supercede the rights of Riga. An actual staple was erected in 1498; Germans forbidden to engage in minor trade and to travel beyond Polozk to Smolensk and Witebsk.

name: Połczyn-Zdrój
Settlement_Description: A German settlement was founded in the 13th century by Benedictine monks from the monastery Stolpe, but a settlement existed before. Duke Bogislaw IV probably built a castle around 1290. First mentioned in a charter in 1331.
Town_Description: Brandenburg town law was most likely granted in 1335 by the sons of Wartislaw IV. It was mentioned as a town in 1337 and was granted Lübeck town law in 1515.

name: Poniec
Toll_Description: King Władysław II ordained in 1398 that merchants had to pay toll in Poniec. Furthermore a toll was levied in 1441 on merchants from Greater Poland.

name: Poppenburg
Settlement_Description: Originally a royal manor at a crossing of the Leine river, which was given to the bishop of Hildesheim in 1049, who erected a castle here (first mentioned in 1227).
Toll_Description: A toll in Poppenburg is first mentioned in 1246. Hildesheim complained in 1459, that a toll was levied on wagon cargoes, where before only toll for horses had to be paid.
Bridge_Description: A bridge existed here before 1291, when it was destroyed by Hildesheim. In 1522, a bridge is mentioned again. In the meantime, the river crossing took place with a ferry.
Ferry_Description: A ferry is mentioned in 1353, 1381 and 1389. Before 1291 and after 1522, there existed a bridge.

name: Poppenbüttel
Settlement_Description: The settlement was first mentioned in 1336.

name: Porz
Toll_Description: The Duke of Berg levied a land toll in 1477. It is possible, however, that a toll had already been levied before this. The toll from 1477 was mentioned as a "new toll". Tariffs and annual revenues are not known.

name: Pretzetze
Settlement_Description: Village and castle, first mentioned in 1328.

name: Poznań
Settlement_Description: Probably a castle existed in the 8th/9th century. Since 968 Poznan was the centre of the bishopric and until 1296 the residence of the Polish dukes. Poznan was first mentioned in 970.
Toll_Description: In 1390, King Władysław of Poland ordained, that the toll tariffs in Sieradz, Kalisz, Pyzdry and Poznań were to be the same as those levied in Piotrków Trybunalski, Łęczyca, Przedecz and Brześć. Prussian merchants complained to Poland about a raise in toll tariffs in Poznań in 1452.
Staple_Description: Staple for the transport of goods from Lithuania, Masovia and the kingdom of Poland. Granted in 1394, and confirmed in the Polish Staple Law of 1565.

name: Potzehne
Settlement_Description: In 1458 the gift of an altar in Kalvörde is confirmed, which came with income from Potzehne.

name: Praha
Toll_Description: Accounts of revenues of tolls in Prague exist for 1311-13 and 1315-23. This was a toll on commodities. In 1331 a wagon toll for the maintenance of the pavement was installed.
Staple_Description: The privilege of King Wenzel II confirmed the staple rights of the old town, with a ban on guest trading and a stay time of five days where guests were obliged to offer their wares for sale. In 1351 trade with foreign merchants in Bohemia and Moravia was restricted to Prague. Staple for wood in Podskal in 1341; expanded to include citizens of the new town in 1356; staple for salt fish established in the new town in 1367. In 1393 further restrictions on guest trading and obligations to use certain roads; repeated in 1415. Staple rights were never complete (they never covered internal Bohemian trade), but they did include an obligation to offer wares for sale. Privileges renewed in 1497 and 1527, but proved difficult to enforce except for the fish staple in the new town which were mentioned again in 1627 and 1649.

name: Pratau
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in a possibly forged document from 966. Mentioned as "urbs" in 1004; the existence of a castle is attested.

name: Preetz
Settlement_Description: A church was built around 1150. In 1226, the settlement was placed under jurisdiction of the Benedictine convent, founded in 1211, which moved to the settlement in 1260. Later the settlement developed into a borough ('flecken'), as which it is characterised in 1513.

name: Pretzsch (Elbe)
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in a falsified charter from 965. The settlement developed from a moated castle that controlled a crossing of the Elbe river. It is mentioned as borough ('Flecken') in 1528 and little town ('Städtlein') in 1533. Formal town statutes were only granted in 1651.

name: Debrzno
Settlement_Description: Mentioned in 1346 when the Teutonic Order donated land to 'in campo Fredeland'.
Town_Description: Grandmaster Winrich von Kniprode granted Kulm town law in 1354.

name: Preußisch Oldendorf
Settlement_Description: The settlement developed from a Carolingian parish. The St. Dionysius' church is mentioned in 996. The settlement acquired borough ('weichbild') privileges in 1692.

name: Pribbenow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1260.

name: Prisser
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1330/52. In 1450, the village consisted of 8 farms, of which one was a mill.

name: Heroldishausen
Toll_Description: Station of secondary safe conduct ('Beigeleitsstelle') of (Großen)Gottern, as mentioned in the regulations of toll and safe conduct for the Amt Langensalza and Thamsbrück from 1516.

name: Princenhage
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in circa 1198, in a fourteenth century copy.

name: Pritzwalk
Settlement_Description: Formerly a Slavic settlement with German immigrants. First mentioned as town in 1256.
Town_Description: Town foundation probably around 1200 by the lords of Putlitz. In 1256 the settlement acquired the town rights of Seehausen from Margraves John and Otto of Brandenburg.

name: Prödel
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1378. Demolished in 1971-1972 to make place for mining activities.

name: Profen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1079. Mentioned in a charter from 1286 as Provin.

name: Prosigk
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1262.
Toll_Description: Secondary station of safe conduct ('Beigeleitsstelle') of Köthen, mentioned in 1563.

name: Przedecz
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station in c. 1349, where 6 gr. 4 den. had to be paid for each horse. In 1390, King Władysław of Poland ordained, that the toll tariffs in Sieradz, Kalisz, Pyzdry and Poznań were to be the same as those levied in Piotrków Trybunalski, Łęczyca, Przedecz and Brześć.

name: Protzen
Settlement_Description: First mention as a parish village in 1324, probably founded at the beginning of the 13th century.

name: Ziegenhain
Settlement_Description: Around 1050 there was a castle at which a settlement developed.
Town_Description: Around 1240 the settlement was mentioned as 'urbs' and 'oppidani' . 1274 mentioned as 'oppidum'.

name: Pühajõe
Settlement_Description: The manor and village were first mentioned in 1241 and belonged to the Teutonic Order from 1426.

name: Puiatu
Settlement_Description: The village belonged to the Dünamünde monastery before 1236.

name: Puide
Settlement_Description: A settlement is already documented in 1218, since a battle of the Germans against Liven and Latvians took place near it. In 1638 it was mentioned as a village.

name: Pulderbos
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1273 is a copy. Next mention in 1299.

name: Purmerend
Settlement_Description: According to Van Berkel & Samplonius, Purmerend is first mentioned in 1342. Cox states that it was already mentioned in 1327.
Town_Description: A castle and town were founded at the site of the old village Purmered by Amsterdam banker Willem Eggert, treasurer of the count of Holland, after 1410. His inhabitants obtained toll-exemption from the countf of Holland in 1412. Between 29 December 1410 and 21 April 1484, Purmerend acquired many town-like features, but there is no single charter that describes an the official grant of town rights. The town acquired further significance as a regional market centre after the draining of the Purmer, Beemster and Wormer lakes in the first half of the 17th century.
Fair_Description: In 1484 (21 apr.) geeft de stadhouder van Holland twee jaarmarkten: 1) 8 dagen na meidag, 2) eerste dag na St. Victor (11 okt.) en een weekmarkt op zaterdag. De prins van Oranje vergunde een jaarlijkse leermarkt in 1575 (24 jan.): eerste maandag na St. Jan te midzomer (24 juni) en daags daarna.

name: Purtse
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1241. In 1421, there is evidence of a manor and a mill.

name: Treia
Settlement_Description: Church village, first mentioned in the 13th century.

name: Kappeln
Settlement_Description: A chapel of St Nicholas is first mentioned in 1357, around which a settlement developed. It was characterised as borough ('flecken') in 1533.

name: Zernikow
Settlement_Description: The manor and village are first mentioned in 1365.

name: Gaworzyce
Toll_Description: King Friedrich III granted Duke Wlodko of Teschen a toll in Gaworzyce in 1452.

name: Pyzdry
Toll_Description: In 1390, King Władysław of Poland ordained, that the toll tariffs in Sieradz, Kalisz, Pyzdry and Poznań were to be the same as those levied in Piotrków Trybunalski, Łęczyca, Przedecz and Brześć.

name: Quakenbrück
Settlement_Description: The castle and settlement are first mentioned in 1188. The place was already called "oppidum" (borough) in 1261. In 1383, older borough ('weichbild') privileges were confirmed by the bishop of Osnabrück.
Town_Description: First mentioned as 'stat' (town) in 1360. The town privileges were derived from those of Osnabrück.
Fair_Description: A fair in Quakenbrück is first mentioned in 1509, but possibly older.
Toll_Description: A wine toll of the bishop of Osnabrück is mentioned in Quakenbrück between 1618 and 1620.

name: Qualitz
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1233.

name: Quarnebeck
Settlement_Description: In 1397 the settlement is sold to the lords of Plathe. This Quarnebeck probably has nothing to do with a settlement of Querenbeke which is mentioned repeatedly in 1311, since this Querenbeke is always mentioned in the context of settlements in the Harz.

name: Quedlinburg
Settlement_Description: The place traces its roots to an old saxonian estate, which is mentioned in 922 as a ludolfing farmyard. In the 10th and 11th century Quedlinburg becomes an important palace for the saxonian kings, after Henry I. is buried here. The saxonian kings like to have their Easter celebration here.
Town_Description: In 1327 the former separated communities of the Old City (founded during 10th century) and the New City (founded during the 12th century) are put together under one council.In 1477 the city succumbs to the regency of the abbess of Quedlinburg monastery, which lets the city lose its autonomy.
Fair_Description: The exact dates of the fairs in Quedlinburg are unknown. One mention occurred in 1585, when a large flood happened during a fair. The exact date of the flood or fair is not mentioned. Because of a plague epidemic a fair on St. Martin's day was cancelled in 1598.

name: Quenstedt
Settlement_Description: King Otto II donated the villa Quenstedi, among others, to Quedlinburg monastery in 992. According to reports from the early 19th century, Quenstedt held the privileges and appearance of a small town quite early, with town walls, a town hall and even a fair. In 1636 during the Thirty Years' War the settlement was utterly destroyed in a fire and was deserted for 14 years, which leads to assume that it couldn't restore its former status.

name: Rastenberg
Settlement_Description: First mention of the castle of Rastenberg in 1282, the residing family is already mentioned in 1252. The village of Rastenberg is first mentioned in 1333.
Town_Description: The village is elevated to town by the Wettins in 1378, but in the 15th century it was probably no more than a market borough (referred to as borough ('Flecken') in 1464). It started to thrive in the 16th century, but was hit hard by the 30-year war.

name: Flarchheim
Toll_Description: Station of secondary safe conduct ('Beigeleitsstelle') of (Großen)Gottern, as mentioned in the regulations of toll and safe conduct for the Amt Langensalza and Thamsbrück from 1516.

name: Hildburghausen
Town_Description: The settlement is first mentioned as "oppidum" in 1307. A council is mentioned in 1314 and Coburg town privileges were granted in 1331.
Fair_Description: The fair of St Michael was moved from Veilsdorf to Hildburghausen in 1331.
Toll_Description: Toll station of the district of Heldburg, for which the oldest accounts date from 1546. Regulations of toll and safe conduct for Hildburghausen remain from 1570.

name: Querfurt
Settlement_Description: The settlement is mentioned in the tithe register of Hersfeld monastery in 899. The castle ("Quernuordiburch") is mentioned in 979.
Town_Description: Town rights are probably granted before 1198.
Fair_Description: A fair was held on the Eselstedt meadow in Querfurt before the Thirty Years' War, which stopped during the war, but was reopened in 1650.
Toll_Description: In 1514 an escort ('Geleitsmann') is mentioned in Querfurt.

name: Räbel
Settlement_Description: A charter mentions the settlement in 946, but it might be a forgery. First secure mention in 1150.

name: Rackith
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in a falsified charter from 966. First certain mention in 1004.

name: Racławice
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station in c. 1349, where 1/2 gr. had to be paid for each horse.

name: Radeburg
Settlement_Description: The origin of the place was the farming village on a ford through the 'Röder', which was built after 1150.

name: Radegast (Zörbig)
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in two records from 1244. Since 1727 the village owned market rights.

name: Radevormwald
Toll_Description: The Duke of Berg levied a land toll around 1459. This toll station is known from a complaint by traders against this very toll. In 1555, the toll was no longer mentioned, which suggests that the toll was removed after the complaint.

name: Radom
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station in a document from c. 1349, where 4 gr. had to be paid for each horse.
Staple_Description: Insignificant staple, confirmed in the Polish staple law of 1565

name: Ranst
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1140, in copy dating from 1265. Next mention in 1148.

name: Ragösen
Toll_Description: Secondary station of safe conduct ('Nebengeleit') of the district ('Amt') Belzig, where it appears in the accounts from 1489 onwards.

name: Züschen
Town_Description: The exact founding of the town is not known, but in 1322 the place was called 'oppidum'. A town seal can be proven in 1363.

name: Radziejów
Toll_Description: A document from probably 1349, a toll in Radziejów is indirectly mentioned.

name: Reiu
Settlement_Description: The village and the manor were probably built around 1200. In 1263, the area around Reidenhof was given to Pernau, in 1520 the entire village was owned by Pernau.

name: Ragow
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1468; several prehistoric finds show that the settlement existed much earlier.

name: Rahula
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1241. During the 16th century it was temporarily in possession of the Teutonic Order ('Deutscher Orden'). In 1586 the village burned down, so that the farmers were resettled.

name: Rambow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1230.

name: Ramlingen
Settlement_Description: The place was first mentioned in 1509.

name: Galluswarte
Settlement_Description: Watchtower in the enclosure ('landwehr') of Frankfurt, built in 1396.

name: Demen
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1265.

name: Rapla
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1241. In 1412 there was a church, mill and a village that were all owned by the Manor of 'Allo'. The village developed into a Borough ('Flecken').

name: Raasiku
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1254. In 1393 it belonged to the monks of Dünamünde and later to the Padis monastery. A hamlet ('Hof') was built in 1497.

name: Kętrzyn
Settlement_Description: A castle built by the Teutonic Order in 1329, a german settlement grew close to it, it was called oppidum in 1345, the first settlement was destroyed by Lithuanians and rebuilt as a fortified town
Town_Description: Johann Schindekopf, the komtur of Balga, granted the new town a handfast with Kulm town law in 1357, it was renewed in 1378

name: Rathenow
Settlement_Description: A German settlement came into being near a castle in the late 12th century. Rathenow is first mentioned as castle district in 1216.
Town_Description: From the 2nd half of the 13th century Rathenow was expanded into a town, during which process the village of Jederitz and the farmstead Rodewalde were incorporated. In 1288 the town ('civitas') received jurisdictional rights, and in 1319 coin rights are granted. Brandenburg town rights are confirmed in 1295.
Fair_Description: During a conflict between the cobblers of Tangermünde and Rathenow, the fairs of Rathenow are mentioned.
Toll_Description: A toll in Rathenow is first mentioned in the survey ('landbuch') of the Mark Brandenburg from 1375, and often mentioned in the 15th century. A shipping toll is first explicitly mentioned in 1559, when a new lock was built in Rathenow. Next to the fee for using the lock, a toll had to be paid.

name: Okonek
Settlement_Description: In 1547 the manor is mentioned in an agreement of exchange. A ducal village was founded by Duke Barnim XI of Pomerania in 1554.
Fair_Description: The place received 2 fairs in 1592, a third in 1597 and a fourth in 1613.

name: Ratzeburg
Settlement_Description: A Slavic castle is first mentioned in 1062. Ratzeburg was a bishopric from 1154 to 1554.
Town_Description: Town privileges were probably granted around 1250. The settlement is first characterised as town in 1261.

name: Rätzlingen
Settlement_Description: In 1311 property in Retzlingen is mentioned as a fiefdom.

name: Raudna
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1241.

name: Friedberger Warte
Settlement_Description: Watchtower in the defensive enclosure ('landwehr') of Frankfurt, built in 1476.

name: Rauschenburg
Toll_Description: A toll was levied on river traffic at the Rauschenburg since ca. 1600.
Ferry_Description: The ferry probably originated around 1310. Later it was replaced by a bridge.

name: Rawa Mazowiecka
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station in a document from c. 1349, where 3 gr. 4 den. had to be paid for each horse.

name: Rawicz
Toll_Description: Old royal Polish border toll station

name: Redderstorf
Settlement_Description: A first mention from 1210 as Ratezbursthorp is uncertain. The village is first certainly mentioned as Ryddagestorpe in 1326.

name: Reddien
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1450/51. An earlier mention from 1330/52 as Reddinghe is uncertain. In 1450, the settlement consisted of 3 farms.

name: Rees
Fair_Description: In 1241 three fairs are mentioned: 1) Sunday after Pentecost, 2) Sept. 7, 3) Sept. 28, each during four days. In 1561 the weekly market was moved from Saturday to Tuesday.
Toll_Description: In 1299, the Archbishop of Cologne gave the town of Rees the right to levy customs on all commodities traded in town as well as a road toll in Rees and Haldern, to fund the maintenance of the roads and the town fortifications. A market toll in Rees was levied by the Elector himself. The privilege was confirmed in 1372 and 1388. The toll was acquired by the Duke of Cleves in 1392.

name: Recz
Settlement_Description: A Pomeranian castle and the castle complex of the Knights Hospitaller that was mentioned in 1269 could be identical. A Cistercian women monastery was built on its ruins in 1296. A Slavic fishing village was located in its vicinity.
Town_Description: The town was founded after 1284 by the Ascanians with Magdeburg town law, to secure the street from Stargard to the east.
Toll_Description: Recz is mentioned as toll and safe conduct station in 1370.

name: Resko
Settlement_Description: A castle was built on an old Slavic fortification in the early 13th century.
Town_Description: Theoderich Horn from Kolberg received the privilege to found a town near the fortification after 1255. The founding privilege with Lübeck town law of the Borcke family from 1282 was endorsed in 1288 by Vidante and his sons.

name: Recke
Settlement_Description: The church village is first mentioned in 1189.

name: Reetz (Görzke)
Settlement_Description: A castle district ('Burgward') is first mentioned in 1161. Later a village.

name: Reher
Settlement_Description: A first mention in 826-876 is not completely certain. The next mention is dated in the mid-13th century.

name: Rehna
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as village in 1230. Before 1236 a Benedictine nunnery was founded. The settlement is characterised as borough ('opidum') in 1362, but it retained the character of a village. A town law is first known from 1791.

name: Rezaka
Settlement_Description: The manor was first mentioned in 1540.

name: Reichenbach
Settlement_Description: This small village was first mentioned in 1140.
Town_Description: The town was founded in the 1240s. In 1274 it was referred to as 'civitas'. The 'Magdeburg Law' is documented for 1367.

name: Reinevere
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1220.

name: Reinerbeck
Settlement_Description: The village was originally called Dudenhausen, first mentioned in 1304-1324. It was probably abandoned in the late Middle Ages. The name Reinerbeck appears first as the name for a stream in 1510. Later the name was transferred to the village.

name: Reinickendorf
Settlement_Description: Probably first founded in 1230, the settlement is first mentioned in 1345. In 1397 it is already property of the twin city of Berlin-Cölln.

name: Reinshagen
Settlement_Description: The church village was first mentioned in 1319.

name: Reinstorf
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1235.

name: Remagen
Toll_Description: 1) From 1317 to 1322, the empire levied a river toll on the Rhine in the course of the 'Barach landfrieden'. In 1473, the Archbishop of Cologne is mentioned as the owner, who moved the toll from Bonn to Remagen for a few weeks. Between 1317 and 1322, 9 Turnosgroschen had to be paid for each foder of wine.<br/>2) The Archbishop of Cologne was mentioned as the holder of the pledge of a land toll from 1421.

name: Remkersleben
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1144 in records of Berge monastery.

name: Remlingen (Wolfenbüttel)
Settlement_Description: The first mention of 986 appears in a falsified charter from 1322. Remains of settlements from the 1st-7th centuries have been found.

name: Remplin
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1283. There existed originally two villages, Magno/Maior ('greater') and Parvo/Minor ('lesser') Remplin.

name: null
Ferry_Description: According to wagoners at the end of the 15th century, a ferry crossing of the Elbe river existed in Riesa.

name: Rendsburg
Settlement_Description: A Danish castle was built on an island in the Eider river at the end of the 11th century; count Adolf II of Holstein erected a border castle on the same location around 1150, which was first mentioned in 1199. Next to it a town developed.
Town_Description: First named as "civitas" in 1253; Lübeck town privileges must have been granted shortly before.
Fair_Description: Heinrich Rantzau mentions a fair on St Matthew's Day in his 1597 description of Schleswig and Holstein. In some years, the fair Kieler Umschlag was held in Rendsburg as well. See Kiel for further information.
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station of the counts of Holstein in 1443 and 1468. Toll accounts are extant for the year 1541-1704, with lacunae in some years (Landesarchiv Schleswig-Holstein, Schleswig).

name: Renkum
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 970, in a copy from 1480. A miraculous image of the Virgin Mary attracted pilgrims from the middle of the 14th century. Duke Reginald IV of Guelders founded a monastery here in 1405.

name: Ritterhude
Settlement_Description: The settlement was first mentioned in 1182.

name: Repnitz
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1366.

name: Reppelin
Settlement_Description: The originally Slavic village is first mentioned in 1256.

name: Rzepin
Town_Description: The Margrave of Brandenburg confirms borders and taxes for the town in 1329. Always called town, except in 1350, when it was mentioned as borough ('opidum')
Toll_Description: A fee for safe conduct ('geleit') of the Margrave of Brandenburg in Reppen is first mentioned in 1335. In 1535, the toll was moved to Frankfurt because of the opening of the new direct connection Frankfurt-Crossen.

name: Reppenstedt
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in 1197. Around 1400, a watchtower of the Lüneburg enclosure ('landwehr') was built here. It was called Uhlenburg/Eulenburg. The complex consisted of a tower, a boom barrier and a bridge over a moat. An inn was mentioned in 1562.

name: Ressen
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 673-691, in a falsified copy from the twelfth century. Mentioned as 'in uilla Rexne' at the end of the eleventh century; as 'Rixne' in 1120 in a twelfth century copy.

name: Tallinn
Settlement_Description: From an early age, the place was a trading center with a natural harbour and a castle. 1219 possibly the first written reference.
Town_Description: The town was founded in 1230 by the settlement of German traders. However, the city consisted of the cathedral-town ('Domstadt') and the lower city ('Unterstadt'). In 1248 the lower town received the Lübeck town law and in 1252 became a member of the Hanseatic League.

name: Rheda
Settlement_Description: The parish of Rheda is first mentioned in 1086/88. A fortification that existed since ca. 1000 was rebuilt as a stone castle from ca. 1170. Next to the castle a borough ('flecken') was built around 1230.
Town_Description: Town privileges were granted in 1355 after the Lippstadt model.

name: Rhede (Ems)
Settlement_Description: The place was mentioned for the first time in 829.
Toll_Description: A land and water toll of the bishop of Münster is mentioned in 1564 complaints, among others of East Frisia and the town Wesel, about the levying of an unusual toll on English cloth in Rhede. The bishop responded that the toll had been levied for a long time and it continued to be levied in the 17th and 18th century.

name: Riskau
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1450/51. A register from 1684 mentioned 6 farms in the village, of which 3 had been abandoned.

name: Rheinberg
Toll_Description: 1) The Archbishop of Cologne owned a river toll on the Rhine here. This was levied in 1235, 1279, from 1286 to 1293, 1298 to 1302 and from 1314. In 1314, 4 Turnosgroschen had to be paid per foder of wine, in 1368 it was 10½ Turnosgroschen. For further tariffs see source. In 1368/69 about 7312 sc. (schild) were collected in the year. For other revenues see source. In the year 1279 there is only referred to a fee for safe conduct, in 1302 a river toll and a fee for safe conduct were mentioned.<br/>2) The town of Rheinberg itself levied land toll in 1235. Tariffs are not known. In 1421/22, 33 mark 5 shillings and 9 denarii were collected. At the same time, a road toll was collected in 1290, which, together with the revenues from the land toll, were used to improve the town's fortifications. In the 15th century, the land toll fell to the Archbishop of Cologne.<br/>3) The road toll was first mentioned in 1290.

name: Rheindorf
Toll_Description: The Count of Berg levied a land toll in 1377. In the same year, ½ alb. per horse had to be paid. In 1411 Rheindorf was a secondary toll station of Mülheim and in 1487 of Dünnwald.

name: Remda
Settlement_Description: First mention in the beginning of the 9th century in the tithe register of the monastery Hersfeld.

name: Rhenen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 855. A hospital is first mentioned in 1383.
Town_Description: Rhenen was granted town privileges between 1250 and 1258. This was probably done by Henry I of Vianden, bishop of Utrecht. Rhenen was walled in 1346.
Fair_Description: Emperor Charles V granted in 1552 (Sept.) a horsefair on 21-23 June. Per horse 3 stuivers should be paid to the emperor, half by the buyer, half by the seller. It is a poor landtown without fairs. There is however a huge pilgrimage for St. Cunea on June 12, where recently 1300 chariots (usually with each four horses) and 12000 horses visited the town. In 1575 there are no horses sold.

name: Ribnitz
Settlement_Description: A castle and court existed in Wendish time. The court and an inn are mentioned in 1210, castle and parish in 1233.
Town_Description: Founded in 1235 by Heinrich Burwyn III of Rostock. Lübeck town privileges were granted in 1257 and have been endorsed multiple times. Merged with nearby Damgarten in 1950.
Toll_Description: Emperor Frederick granted a new toll to the dukes of Mecklenburg in Ribnitz in 1471, which led to protests of Wismar, Rostock and Lübeck. Lübeck was exempted in 1473.

name: Riemsloh
Settlement_Description: The place was first mentioned in 1160.

name: Ristiküla
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1442.

name: Riisipere
Settlement_Description: In 1394 a farm in "Rysenberge" was mentioned. In 1598 the place was divided into Old- and New-Riesenberg ('Alt- und Neu-Riesenberg').They were reunited in 1669.

name: Prabuty
Settlement_Description: The Old Prussian castle was destroyed in 1236, a castle for the bishop of Pomesania was built between 1330 and 1340
Town_Description: The brother of the bishop of Pomesania was the locator of the new town and granted the founding documents between 1285 and 1321, bishop Rudolf himself granted a renewed handfast with Kulm town law in 1330

name: Heel
Settlement_Description: The settlement goes back to the Roman settlement Catualium, first mentioned in ca. 365 (in a 13th-century copy).

name: Riesa
Settlement_Description: Originally a Slavic village, German settlement since the middle of the 12th century. A Benedictine monastery was founded in 1119, which is the first mention of the settlement. It developed into a market borough ('marktflecken') in the 16th century.
Town_Description: Town privileges were granted by Johann Georg I. in 1623.

name: Rheine
Settlement_Description: The settlement, going back to a Carolingian 'villa', was first mentioned in 838.
Town_Description: Rheine received Münster town rights from bishop Ludwig II in 1327. They were partially limited in 1627 and extended again in 1632.
Fair_Description: The oldest evidence for fairs in Rheine dates from 1450, when two fairs are mentioned on Dedication Day on the Sunday after the Assumption of Mary and the "cold market" before Christmas. In 1484, two additional fairs are mentioned, on St Dionysius and All Saints' Day.

name: Riemst
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1066, in an eighteenth century copy. Next mention in 1096.

name: Rīga
Settlement_Description: The settlement was founded in 1201 by Bishop Albert. The first episcopal palatinate was built before 1234. Shortly after 1202 a castle of the Teutonic Order was built, which was destroyed by the Rigans in 1297. A new castle was therefore built in 1330.
Town_Description: German citizens from Gotland and Germany received Gotland town rights in 1211 and Hamburg town rights in 1294/97. In 1350, however, they got their own Rigian town privileges.
Staple_Description: Staple for the trade along the River Duna. The ban on trade in the Semgaller region [?] formed the basis of the Riga staple. In 1229 all merchants given free passage along the Duna, but privilege withdrawn in the 14th century. Overseas merchants not allowed to trade with Smolensk via the Duna, while Russian and Lithuanian merchants not allowed to trade in the Baltic via the Duna. Riga reported to Lübeck in 1468 a ban on guest trading in their city (HR II, 6 n 143). From 1406 merchants from Polozk free from the Riga staple; in return (until 1498) merchants from Riga freed from the Polozk staple.

name: Rijnsburg
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 918-948, in a eleventh century copy. Next mention dates from the beginning of the eleventh century.

name: Rijssen
Settlement_Description: Archaeological finds show that there was a settlement already around the beginning of the Common Era. A permanent settlement probably existed from around 900 onwards. First mentioned in 1188 (in a late 13th-century copy).
Town_Description: Town privileges granted by Otto III of Holland, bischop of Utrecht, in 1243.
Fair_Description: In the town privileges of 1243, Rijssen acquired the right to organise two fairs and two weekly markets. Dates and duration of the fairs, however, are unknown.

name: Ringelheim
Settlement_Description: Ringelheim was seat of a local court. In the 10th century, a monastery of canonesses was built here, which was converted to a Benedictine monastery in 1154. The Reformation was introduced in 1568, but it became Catholic again in 1643.
Toll_Description: A toll and safe conduct of the bishop of Hildesheim in Ringelheim was cancelled in 1354. In accounts of the town of Hildesheim, a new toll in Ringelheim is mentioned in 1455, where citizens of Hildesheim had been toll-free before. However, already in 1444 toll for commodities in Ringelheim had also been paid for by Hildesheim.

name: Rõngu
Settlement_Description: In the 14th/15th century a castle was built, which was first mentioned in 1413. It was burned down in 1558, so that a new castle was built. A village was first mentioned in 1582.

name: Drechow
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as part of the name Rodolfus de Drechowe in 1250. The settlement itself is first mentioned in 1269.

name: Rittermannshagen
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1260.

name: Röa
Settlement_Description: The manor and village were mentioned in 1558. In 1639 there was an estate.

name: Rijswijk
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention probably at the end of eleventh century, in a copy from circa 1420.

name: Röbel/Müritz
Settlement_Description: Castle and village existed around 1200, first mentioned in 1239.
Town_Description: Next to the already existing settlement, a town was founded by the Lords of Werle in the first half of the 13th century. In 1261, Schwerin town privileges were confirmed for both - now united - parts of the settlement.

name: Röblingen am See
Settlement_Description: Mentioned  in the Hersfelder Zehntverzeichnis in 890. Later a ministerial family of Röblingen is mentioned, which is unrelated with the dynasty of Röblingen.

name: Roodu
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1241 and was abandoned since 1694. During the 15th century the place belonged to the Teuntonic Order.

name: Meerkerk
Fair_Description: A horsefair is found in the 16th century with Viti en Modestidag (June 15). In 1535-'38 there is a difference about the toll-exemption of Gorinchem. The toll-keeper of Gorinchem (72 jaar old) said that it was never levied. Old skippers say that only a bridge-toll existed. In 1561/2 toll, ferry and bridge-toll together were leased out by the steward of the lord of Brederode for almost 47 pounds. The toll levied at the horse-market is also mentioned but without an amount.
Bridge_Description: In 1535-'38 there is a difference about the toll-exemption of Gorinchem. The toll-keeper of Gorinchem (72 jaar old) said that it was never levied. Old skippers say that only a bridge-toll existed. In 1561/2 toll, ferry and bridge-toll together were leased out by the steward of the lord of Brederode for almost 47 pounds. The bridge crossed the Oude Zederik at Lakerveld (see there).
Ferry_Description: In 1535-'38 there is a difference about the toll-exemption of Gorinchem. The toll-keeper of Gorinchem (72 jaar old) said that it was never levied. Old skippers say that only a bridge-toll existed. In 1561/2 toll, ferry and bridge-toll together were leased out by the steward of the lord of Brederode for almost 47 pounds. The ferry crossed the Oude Zederik at Lakerveld (see there).

name: Straupe
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1221/24. The castle was probably built in 1263. 1408 Klein Roop ('Mazstraupe') was separated.
Town_Description: The fortified borough ('Hakelwerk') was referred to as town in 1356 and received town rights of Riga in 1374.

name: Rogäsen
Settlement_Description: At the end of the 14th century mention as Ragoesen, in the property of the noble family of Werder for 500 years.

name: Rogätz
Settlement_Description: In 1144 the village passed from the counts of Hillersleben to the bishops of Havelberg.

name: Roggentin
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1219.

name: Rooküla
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1241 and was located on an old winter road ('Winterstraße'). A hamlet ('Hof') was built between 1636 and 1684.

name: Rohrberg
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1212 as a town ('civibus') with citizens ('cives'), but after that only ever referred to as village.

name: Roela
Settlement_Description: Manor and hamlet ('Hof') that were both built in the middle of the 16th century.

name: Rolde
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in circa 1232, in a  seventeenth century copy. The church village was located on an intersection of roads towards Groningen, Coevorden and Meppel.

name: Rauna
Settlement_Description: The castle was probably built in 1262, but only mentioned in 1381. In 1471 a fortified borough ('Hakelwerk') was mentioned.
Town_Description: The fortified borough ('Hakelwerk') was referred to as a minor town and received town rights of Riga later. They were confirmed in 1590.

name: Renda
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1230/31 and was acquired by the Teutonic Order in 1253.

name: Ronnenberg
Settlement_Description: The place was first mentioned in 1073.

name: Rotenburg (Wümme)
Settlement_Description: Bishop Rudolf of Verden built the castle Rotenburg around 1195, next to which a settlement developed. In the 15th century it was characterised a borough ('weichbild') as well as minor town ('städtchen'). In 1403, Bishop Conrad III von Verden granted borough rights ('weichbildrechte'), which were extended in 1427.

name: Roosendaal
Settlement_Description: Roosendaal is first mentioned in 1268. It was elevated to city rank on 3 May 1809 by Louis Bonaparte, king of Holland. This elevation, however, lasted only untill 1814.
Fair_Description: In 1552 the magistrate of the village Rosendale asked the prince of Orange, as there were passing a lot of horses from Holland, permission for two horse- and other cattlefairs like in Hoogstraten. One to be organised in Spring, one in Autumn. There were already two fairs, one the day after the 'Kermis' (carnival) and one after St. John Baptist (June 24), each to be freed for eight days. As there came much flax and other measurable merchandise they asked for a weigh-house. They also asked permission to install a roadtoll, like in Bergen (op Zoom) and Oudenbosch and elswehere is asked from them. As 'straatgeld' (street-tax) per barrel beer 1/2s. is levied to maintain the big paved roads. In 1572 (Jan. 25) a yearly horsefair is granted on Sept. 20 and the next days, when paying  6 'Arthois' of each 40 groten.

name: Susz
Settlement_Description: A castle mound existed close to the town before it was founded.
Town_Description: The founding documents of 1305, granted by the Pomesanian diocesan chapter, are lost. They were renewed with Kulm town law in 1314.

name: Rosmalen
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in circa 800-850, in a copy dating from 1170-1175. Next mention in 1295.

name: Roßbach
Settlement_Description: First mention as 'Rozpach' in 1057. First mention of a manor house in 1196. A parish village with two churches in the Middle Ages, it became the scene of a major battle during the Seven Year's War in 1757, during which the French had to suffer a defeat.

name: Roßlau
Settlement_Description: Located at the confluence of the rivers Rossel and Elbe. A Slavic moated castle is attested here. The noble house of Roßlau is first mentioned in 1215.
Town_Description: First mentioned as a town in 1382. In 1685 also referred to as borough ('flecken').

name: Roßwein
Settlement_Description: Previously Slavic fishing village, which was settled by Germans in the 12th century. At the end of the 12th century, a margravial-Meissen manor.

name: Rostock
Settlement_Description: A Wendish village was destroyed in 1160 after a dispute with Waldemar I of Denmark. Soon after a market settlement of German merchants developed.
Town_Description: Lord Heinrich Borwin I of Mecklenburg endorsed the Lübeck town law in 1218. The three different parts of town were united in 1265. The local university was founded in 1419.
Fair_Description: A letter from the 12th of January 1390 from Rostock to Zutphen provides the first reference to the Pentecost market in Rostock. The market developed into an important fair in northern Europe by the 17th century.
Staple_Description: Staple for stockfish from Bergen; in 1446 members of the Hanse only allowed to export flour, malt, and other victuals to Bergen if they brought fish from Bergen back with them to Lübeck, Wismar, Rostock or Stralsund. Regulations from the 15th century indicate a ban on guest trading.

name: Rotselaar
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1140, in a copy dating from circa 1265.

name: Rotterdam
Settlement_Description: Rotterdam is first mentioned in the period 1280-1287. Rotterdam originates from two seperate settlements, each on either side of the River Rotte. Together, these former settlements make up Rotterdam. In the fourteenth century, Rotterdam grows into a town-like settlement. A hospital is first found in 1329.
Town_Description: Rotterdam was already granted town rights in 1299; however, this grant was soon withdrawn. In the grant of 7 June 1340, by William IV, count of Holland (William II, count of Hainaut), no mention is made of earlier town privileges. One of the smaller ‘Kamers’ (departments) of the VOC (Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie, Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602) was located in Rotterdam.
Fair_Description: The old town-right of 1340 stated two fairs of each 8 days, whenever they liked it. The comital account of 1343/'4 mentions a market-toll with St. Margaret (July 13): 5 lb. 2sc., and with St. Bartholomeus (August 24): 50 sc. In 1363 the last one is altered to: Mary Magdalenaday (July 22). In 1412 the town obtained two free fairs of each 14 days: 1) St. Margaret, 2) St. Bartholomeus. The town had to pay count Willem 6 pound yearly for this. In 1472 this fee is bought off from Charles the Bold. The early 15th century charterbook mentions two fairs of each 14 days, 1) first Sunday after H. Ascensioens day (Ascension), on Wednesday afterwards the first 'toochdag' (display day) of horses and other goods from of old, 2): O.L.V. dag Assumptio (August 15), 4 days later on August 19 the first toochdag of horses. The location of the fair for horses is in the Lombardtstraat on de Meent next  to the chapel. Yields of the farming out of both the market-tolls are edited for the years 1344-1479. In 1565 (August) king Philip II granted a free fair for leather, to compensate the huge fire of 1563. In 1580 (Jan. 21) surrrounding towns react on the request of Rotterdam dated 1579 29 Oct. for a free seed-fair. On 28 May king Philip II granted a free fair for seeds and leather, in order to compensate the decaying fishery and drapery as a result of the war. Dates: August 12 for 8 days. Regarding this an agreement with Delft was made on May 16.

name: Rottorf
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in a charter of the monastery of St Michael in Lüneburg from 1233.

name: Roxförde
Settlement_Description: The name already occurs in a border description from 786, but in this case a lake or a body of water is referred to. The existence of a settlement can not be ruled out. First secure mention in 1400.

name: Rozprza
Toll_Description: A toll is first mentioned in 1136.

name: Rottleberode
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 968. In Ottonian times an important royal court on the way from Wallhausen to Quedlinburg. A market is mentioned in 994.

name: Rühn
Settlement_Description: Cistercian monastery, founded by bishop Brunward of Schwerin in 1232.

name: Ruhrort
Settlement_Description: Around 1300, there existed a fishermen's settlement on the Rhine island Werth. A castle was constructed here between 1372 and 1380, to secure a toll station.
Town_Description: Ruhrort is first mentioned as town in 1551.
Toll_Description: Count Johann of Moers acquired the right to levy a toll of 4 Turnosen of each fuder wine on an island in the Rhine from Emperor Charles IV in 1371. The toll was shared with the count of Mark in 1372, who constructed the castle Ruhrort to secure the toll station. In 1373, the toll fee was raised to 6 Turnosen. Although the toll was cancelled 1379, the toll rights were confirmed in 1398. The Mark part of the toll was moved to Orsoy between 1405 and 1422. Citizens of Ruhrort were exempted from toll payments in 1437.

name: Ruila
Settlement_Description: Village that was sold to the Teutonic Order ('Deutscher Orden') in 1346. In the 16th century it was an anbandoned place.

name: Ruinen
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1139, in a sixteenth century copy.

name: Rūjiena
Settlement_Description: A castle was built between 1260 and 1270. This was about 3 km west of today's town, but was destroyed in 1560. Around the same time that the castle was built, a church was built on the northern bank of the Ruje river.In 1461 a settlement that belonged to the castle was mentioned and was referred to as 'oppidum' in 1516.
Town_Description: In 1516, Rujen was referred to as 'oppidum'.

name: Fahre
Settlement_Description: The settlement was first mentioned in 1505. At the ferry, there existed an inn and a chapel. The inn was mentioned in 1575.

name: Rümpel
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1342. Also named Groß Rümpel in the 15th century, to discern it from Klein Rümpel (currently Höltenklinken).

name: Rüningen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 780-802. On a hill east of the village, the watchtower Rüninger Turm was erected in 1385, which guarded the defensive enclosure ('landwehr') of the town Braunschweig.

name: Rüssel
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in a charter from 977.

name: Rüssen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in a charter of the monastery Corvey from the beginning of the 11th century.

name: Rucava
Settlement_Description: In 1253 the settlement was assigned to the Teutonic Order.

name: Ruurlo
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention forged circa 1118-1127. Next mention in 1180-1190.

name: Rüthnick
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1422.

name: Zalewo
Town_Description: The founding of the town was started by the Teutonic Order komtur of Christburg, Hinrich Zuckschwert between 1299 and 1301, the founding documents with Kulm town lw were signed by the komtur Gegehard von Schwarzburg in 1305, they were renewed in 1320 and expanded in 1334

name: Sakla
Settlement_Description: Originally a village called "Sakull" in the region 'Wacke'. Around 1750 the village became 'Kronsgut'.

name: Saarde
Settlement_Description: In the middle of the 16th century a church was built and a pastorate was established. The church fell into disrepair in 1613-42, so a new one was built in 1642 and was called 'Saara'.

name: Jäärja
Settlement_Description: Originally a hamlet ('Wirtschaftshof') and manor of the Teutonic Order, which was built around 1442. In 1560 this was burned down by the Russians.

name: Saarmund
Settlement_Description: Mention of a castle in 1217, which was probably based on a Slavic fortification. Around the castle a settlement developed which never acquired town rights (referred to as opydulum in 1375), but had some significance as a marketplace and toll station.
Toll_Description: In 1364 and 1365 it was confirmed that merchants from Berlin and Cölln were exempted from the margravial transit toll in Saarmund. The toll is mentioned again in 1576.

name: Žatec
Toll_Description: In 1336 a toll on floated wood on the Ohře is mentioned in Žatec.

name: Sabel (Rostock)
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1307.

name: Sachau
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1388/1440. The settlement is mentioned as abandoned in 1472, but it was repopulated by 1506.

name: Rautela
Settlement_Description: <b>Inn:</b> An inn was established in Rautela in 1600, and Frans Markunpoika was appointed as the innkeeper. Since the inn was so close to Pyöli inn, and only operated for two years, they might have been working together.

name: Sachsenburg
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1132, but the place has been continuously settled at least since the late Bronze Age. The two castles Sachsenburg and Hakenburg controlled the important road through the narrow valley of the Unstrut river, known as Thüringer Pforte (Thuringian gate).
Toll_Description: According to the "Verzeichnis der Knechte und Tore", deliveries of salt had to be brought via the toll in Sachsenburg and Herbsleben to the Johannis gate in Erfurt. In 1394 landgrave Balthasar of Meißen gave the countess Adelheid of Beichlingen the "toll under the house of Sachsenburg" (<i>"czoll under dem huse czu der Sachsenburg"</i>). In 1404 the safe conduct of Sachsenburg is mentioned. Trade from Franken and Nuremberg to the seaside towns in Germany was lead via the Sachsenburg pass. The toll was paid north and south of the bridgehead. With Erfurt's economically weakened position to Leipzig, the forced usage of the road via Sachsenburg is increased. Toll and safe conduct tariffs remain from before 1520 and 1654/55, printed in Straube.

name: Sangaste
Settlement_Description: The manor was founded in 1287 and served as the summer residence of the bishops of Dorpat. The former St. Andreas church was built in the 14th century and was part of the parish 'Theal-Fölk'.

name: Zagórze
Bridge_Description: A bridge in Zagórze is mentioned in 1342.

name: Dolní Zálezly
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station on the Elbe at the beginning of the 17th century, with an imperial and a municipal toll.

name: Salacgrīva
Settlement_Description: The fishing village was first mentioned in 1215. The term 'vicus Salis' was used in 1432, but it is unclear whether it referred to Salismünde or Alt Salis (today: 'Vecsalaca').
Town_Description: 1512/16 minor town rights ('Weichbildrechte') 'thor Salcza' were granted. In 1519 the term 'oppidulum' was found. The granting of city rights has not been documented.

name: Salzbergen
Settlement_Description: The place was first mentioned in 1172.

name: Bad Salzdetfurth
Settlement_Description: Because of the existence brine sources, saltworks developed in the 12th century. Around 1392 the settlement had the seal of a market borough ('marktflecken'), although is also referred to in the sources as village or town.

name: Salzgitter-Bad
Settlement_Description: The saltworks Salzliebenhalle near the village Gitter are first mentioned around 1125. The settlement near the saltworks is first called "Solte to Gittere"; the name Salzgitter appears in 1459.
Town_Description: Around 1400, Salzgitter became a town. In the 15th century a council and town seal are attested. However, the town lost its independent position when it became part of the duchy Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel in 1523.

name: Salzhemmendorf
Settlement_Description: Saltworks near Hemmendorf are first mentioned in 1169; a settlement developed here in the 13th century.

name: Leppäkoski
Settlement_Description: <b>Inn:</b> An inn was established in Leppäkoski in 1636.

name: Salzkotten
Settlement_Description: During the translation of the relics of St. Liborius to Paderborn in 836, they stopped at the Heder, where there were several small settlements. From the 11th century onwards, a larger settlement developed around the area of the brine springs with the cottages of the salt manufacturers, which was first mentioned as "locus salis" in 1160.
Town_Description: The location on the border between the archbishopric of Cologne and the bishopric of Paderborn, the salt boiling industry and the Hellweg running near by favoured the development of the town. In 1247, the Bishop of Paderborn raised Salzkotten to the status of a town and had the salt boiling district fortified. After several feuds between Cologne and Paderborn, the town was divided between the two parties in 1256, enlarged to double its size and the Hellweg now led through it. The division led to further disputes, which ended with the archbishop's withdrawal in 1294.

name: Bad Salzuflen
Settlement_Description: The salt deposits in Salzuflen were already known in prehistoric times, but are first mentioned only in 1036-1051.
Town_Description: In 1322 a burgomaster and town council first appear in a document, and the settlement is characterised as borough ('wygbold'). After the settlement and its surroundings were destroyed in the Soest feud in 1447, the town was reconstructed and expanded and the town privileges were reaffirmed in 1488.

name: Järva-Jaani
Settlement_Description: In 1221/23 the Danes started building a church in the village of 'Kettis' (now Keika). They completed the building by the end of the 13th century. A parish was established.

name: Harju Jaani
Settlement_Description: The church was built in the early 14th century. The associated pastorate was established at the same time. The place where the church is today is called Raasiku.

name: Sandau
Settlement_Description: In the 10th century a settlement probably already existed, but is first mentioned as 'villa' between 1184 and 1192.
Town_Description: In 1272 the settlement was granted ferry rights and other privileges and was first referred to as town. A council is mentioned in 1308. Probably in 1322 the town was fortified. The settlement remained a small agrarian town ('Ackerbürgerstädtchen'), however. It lost part of its legal autonomy in 1634.
Toll_Description: In 1425 archbishop Günther pawned Sandau and its tolls and safe conduct to the bishop of Havelberg. Further mention of the toll in a quarrel between the city of Magdeburg and the archbishop in 1432, and during negotiations of the tolls of Klietz, Jerichow and Sandau on the diet of princes in 1480-1490.

name: Sandersleben
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1046 in a donation charter by Henry III to Meißen monastery (MGH DD H III, nr. 157).
Town_Description: Town privileges since the beginning of the 14th century. New town privileges were granted in 1497 after a fire had completely destroyed the town.

name: Sandhatten
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as "Westhathen" in 1240; mentioned as "Sandhatten" since 1324.

name: Sandkrug (Oldenburg)
Settlement_Description: The hamlet ('bauerschaft') was originally called Streek and first mentioned in 1526. In the 18th century, the inn and post station Sandkrug on the post road Oldenburg-Bremen was erected here, which later became the official name for the settlement.

name: Sandrup
Settlement_Description: First mentioned between 1022 and 1023. The road crossed the defensive enclosure ('landwehr') of Münster here, which was closed with a boom barrier.

name: Sankt Georgsberg
Settlement_Description: A Benedictine monastery was founded around 1044, destroyed by a Slavic revolt in 1066, and refounded around or before 1143. The parish church became the regional centre of the christianisation.

name: Sankt Goar
Toll_Description: The Count of Katzenelnbogen probably levied a river toll on the Rhine even before 1219 until 1235. In 1245, the toll was established again. From the year 1368 it is known that 10 turnosgroschen had to be paid per  foder of wine. In 1480/81 about 1822 gulden were collected, in 1481/82 about 1051 gulden, in 1482/83 about 3209 gulden and in 1485 about 3017 gulden. For further revenues see source.

name: Pärnu-Jaagupi
Settlement_Description: A church was mentioned in 1325. A settlement developed around the St. Jakobi church at the end of the 19th century.

name: Sankt-Jacobshof
Settlement_Description: The leper hospital of St James (Jakob) first appears in a register of the town Wismar around 1250. It was the successor of the hospital of St George, which was located more to the east. The chapel was demolished in 1631, the last leper died in 1639 and the poor house was demolished in 1675. The connected farm, however, remained in existence.

name: Sankt Jürgen
Settlement_Description: In 1392 an infirmary is mentioned on the road between Groß Salze and Frohse on the street to Schönebeck. Its exact location cannot be reconstructed today.

name: Katrinas
Settlement_Description: The place belonged to the parish of the same name. It had a church that was built in 1624.

name: Kadrina
Settlement_Description: The parish was established in the 13th or 14th century. The borough ('Flecken') developed in the 19th century.

name: Maarja-Magdaleena
Settlement_Description: The parish was first mentioned in 1443. In the 19th century, a borough ('Flecken') developed around the church.

name: Koeru
Settlement_Description: The parish was founded in the second half of the 13th century.

name: Skulte
Settlement_Description: The church itself was built even before 1646. It is known that it was rebuilt in 1646. The village and manor 'Skulte' ('Adjamünde') was first mentioned in 1540.

name: Järva-Madise
Settlement_Description: St. Matthäi is a parish that has been mentioned regularly since the 15th century. However, it appears under other names, such as 'Goldenberge' (1467) or 'Kullenbeck'. Baptisms have already been documented for 1220. The St. Matthäi church was built in the 14th century and was first mentioned in 1427.

name: Sankt Mauritz
Settlement_Description: St. Mauritz Abbey was founded in 1080, probably on an older farming ground.

name: Pēterupe
Settlement_Description: The originally wooden church was built in 1641. Today, it belongs to 'Saulkrasti' ('Neubad').

name: Peetri
Settlement_Description: The village and the parish of the same name already existed at the beginning of the 13th century. The church was probably built in 1221-23.

name: Saraiķi
Settlement_Description: The village and manor of the Teutonic Order was named in 1291 together with the stream of the same name.

name: Sarstedt
Settlement_Description: First mentioned between 1046 and 1056 and mentioned in 1216 as farm of the bishop of Hildesheim. Bishop Conrad II built a castle in Sarstedt in 1221-1225.
Town_Description: Before 1296, the settlement was reconstructed and expanded and acquired town privileges from bishop Siegfried II of Hildesheim. From 1319, the settlement is called "civitas". Citizens of Sarstedt were exempted from all taxes to the bishop's bailiff by bishop Heinrich III in 1350.
Toll_Description: A toll of the bishop of Hildesheim in Sarstedt is mentioned among others in 1388 and 1441. It is unclear whether this is the same toll as the one on the "Bruch vor Sarstedt" (Bierbruch) mentioned in 1384.

name: Bad Sassendorf
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1169-1179. Saltworks already existed at that time.

name: Sassenheim
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 918-948, in a eleventh century copy. Next mention dates from the beginning of the eleventh century.

name: Saula
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1241. The place was owned by the manor Kose.
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Pirita existed in 1423, and was probably not built before 1346.

name: Saunstorf
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1230.

name: Sawin
Toll_Description: A toll on Ruthenian salt was introduced by the king of Poland in 1504.

name: Sattelpaß
Settlement_Description: Border station with a guardsman, first mentioned in 1545. Sattelpass was the end of the safe conduct of Coburg. Until the 19th century location of a bar gate.

name: Rabenstein
Settlement_Description: The castle Rabenstein is first mentioned in 1251, but it was probably built in the 12th century. It changed owner and was destroyed several times during the Middle Ages and Early Modern times but is used until today.

name: Svendborg
Settlement_Description: There is archaeological evidence of a permanent settlement with an urban character in the first half of the 12th century. Presumably the settlement developed around a castle. Both castle and settlement may have been founded by the Slavic magnate Knud Prislavsøn, who was a vassal of king Valdemar I the Great (1157-1182) of Denmark.
Town_Description: Town privileges granted by king Valdemar II the Victorious (1202-1241). The castle of Svendborg is first mentioned in 1229, but appears to have been demolished soon after. Perhaps because the town was fortified in the 13th century. Townsmen are documented in 1408, a town hall in 1469 and a town council in 1477. There can be no doubt, however, that these urban institutions were already introduced before the 15th century.
Fair_Description: Svendborg presumably had at least one annual fair. The age and exact character of the fair is unknown. The fair had a local character, and at the end of the 17th century, it was held on the 17th july.

name: Mühlenbrücke
Bridge_Description: A draw bridge across the Wakenitz is first mentioned in 1160, which was a predecessor of the current Mühlenbrücke (mill bridge).

name: Bavay
Settlement_Description: In the Roman period situated on a crossing of landroads and called Bagacum.
Fair_Description: A fair is found in 1265. Privileges granted by duke Albert of Bavaria and his son William IV were burnt in 1422 but confirmed in 1425-'34 and consisted a.o. of two free fairs with Bouhourdy or grand carȇme (great Lent: before Eastern) and with St. Michael (Sept. 29) and a free weekly market.

name: Werf
Toll_Description:
The 'Brabantse toll' or 'Grote Watertol' was levied at the Werf from merchants outside Brabant and amounted 1% of all goods imported or exported Antwerp. A tariff from this 'grote watertol' dated 1550 is edited. Yields of the 'grote watertol' between 1396-1549 are collected.
The socalled 'Riddertol' or small toll was also levied at the Werf and consisted of two parts: levied from 'droge waren' (goods like wool, cheese but also from each ship with a rudder) and from 'natte waren' (goods like wine, beer). The first part also consisted of the 'joktol' levied from the goods on horses or wagons, the 'waaggeld' (money to be paid at the weigh-house) and the tithes from fish levied during Lent. These tolls were owned by the duke of Brabant but for the most part given in long lease to several knights and nobility. Income from this small toll was roughly 1/4 of the 'Grote tol' and both rights were farmed out or collected together.
A tariff from the 'joktol' (goods transported over land) and the 'riddertol' (aboard on ships) dated 1242 is edited. In 1365 a toll on the 'burchtwerk' was installed by the lord of the town. This toll had to be paid by towns in Brabant. Aarschot Herentals, Lier, Mechelen, Vilvoorde and somewhat later Turnhout bought this toll off. Accounts from the toll dated 1365-1404 are edited. Exempt were a.o. Aachen, Zoutleeuw, 's-Hertogenbosch, Heusden and the countship Flanders. A tariff dated 1296 indicates contacts with the Baltic-area.
Harbour_Description:
The centre of the harbour of Antwerpen was formed by the so-called Werf ('wharf') or Kranenhoofd ('crane head'), a protruding bank in the Scheldt river at the oldest core of the city. A crane is first mentioned here in 1263. Smaller vessels also moored along other parts of the city's waterfront and in the many canals. During the trading boom of the 16th century, the harbour capacity became insufficient and ships sometimes had to wait for weeks before they could unload at the harbour.
In the second half of the 16th century there were some 70 shipbuilders. The Antwerp fleet consisted mostly of medium-sized and small ships, also usuful for the inland trade on the rivers in Brabant with ultimate destinations in Zoutleeuw and Tienen. In Flanders regular connections existed with Baasrode, Dendermonde and further towards Ieper. More often also with the harbours in Holland and Zeeland.

name: Bad Doberan
Settlement_Description: The Cistercian monastery Doberan, founded in 1171 at the site of the current village Althof, was named after the nearby Slavic village Doberan. The monastery was destroyed in 1179 and rebuilt at its current location, the old village of Doberan, in 1186. From 1218 a market settlement developed, that was referred to as borough ('flecken') in 1611. Town privileges were only granted in 1879.

name: Findenwirunshier
Settlement_Description: Findenwirunsheir, a corruption from the Slavic Vinzire, is first mentioned in 1496. A water mill was located here. In 1843 it was merged with the new settlement Neu Kaliß.

name: Ameide
Fair_Description: In 1521 the fair is 14 days before St. Johsday in the Summer (June 24). The borders of the freedom are above the cross above Bergstoep below Ammers (next to Schoonhoven) and for those who came from upstream below Culemborg past the 'watersloot'. This is written in a tollregister of Schoonhoven and Gorinchem.Verkerk mentiones the 'market toll' in 1784, it was also called 'silent toll'.The toll was levied from 18th of June to July 20th another souce says from 20th of June to July  20th.
Toll_Description: The history of this toll for sailing transport is rather unknown. In 1400 there is struggle against Lord Jan van Arkel who levies toll on the river Lek in Ameide. We know some other details from the lawsuit between Utrecht and the Lord of Brederode that was finished in 1534. The Lord of Brederode claimed that his family owned the toll for more than 60 years before 1516. Utrecht put forward incorrect but unnoticed a charter dated 975 which referred to 'Amuda' (Muiden). In 1534 Utrecht was declared toll-exempt by the Grote Raad and the lord of Brederode had to pay 900 pounds for in 1516 unjust arrested goods. In 1545 another lawsuit was put forward at the 'Grote Raad of Mechelen' by Schoonhoven about the incorrect toll at Ameide. In 1546 Schoonhoven obtained toll-exemption at Ameide from the lord of Brederode, both on land and water when showing their 'tolbrief' (letter of exemption).
Harbour_Description: In 1351 Ameide obtained toll-exemption from the count of Holland.

name: Otava
Settlement_Description: <b>Inn:</b> An inn was established in Otava in 1584.

name: Sayda
Town_Description: Already mentioned as 'oppidum' in 1250. Referred to as  'civitas' in 1289. A town charter ('Stadtbrief') was issued in 1442, but town regulations ('Städteordnung') were only adopted in 1834.
Toll_Description: First mentioned as toll station in 1324. The regulations of safe conduct from 1550 state that if a wagon with garlic passes, it has to pay some garlic (LHASA, MD, d. 45, A Nr. 146 II, Amt Seyda 1550.).

name: Schellerten
Settlement_Description: Between 1235 and 1261 the settlement was first mentioned.

name: Schaafhausen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1360. According to a 1684 register, the settlement consisted of 4 half farms, of which one was abandoned.

name: Schaarbeek
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1120, in a copy from the end of thirteenth century.

name: Schafstädt
Settlement_Description: Settlement from ancient Thuringian ('altthüringisch') times, mention in the Hersfelder Zehntverzeichnis from the end of the 9th century.
Town_Description: Town rights were probably granted in 1539 and confirmed in 1558.
Toll_Description: Secondary station of safe conducht ('Beigeleitsstelle') of Lauchstädt.

name: Schardam
Settlement_Description: A dam was built to separate the Beemster lake from the Zuiderzee around 1315 and was first mentioned in 1319. Next to it, a village developed.
Lock_Description: Count Willem V of Holland granted permission to build a lock in the dam in 1357.

name: Scharfoldendorf
Settlement_Description: The place was first mentioned in 1146.

name: Scharlibbe
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1351 as the property of a Johann of Buch.

name: Scharnhop
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1307. In the 14th century, it was a village with 7 farms; in 1568 there was only a farm of a manor ('meyerhof') left.

name: Scharpzow
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1229.

name: Scharzfeld
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 952, in a falsified document from the 13th century.

name: Scharn
Settlement_Description: The earliest mentions from 1145 and 1151 appear to be forgeries. The next mention dates from c. 1179-1180.

name: Scheeren
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1345, it is deserted in 1521. In 1686 an inn and sheep farms are mentioned.

name: Schenefeld (Steinburg)
Settlement_Description: First mentioned by Adam of Bremen in the late 11th century, who described the foundation of a missionary church here in ca. 825. Although it always remained a village, Schenefeld developed into a significant political and economic centre for the region.

name: Schenefeld (Pinneberg)
Settlement_Description: Around 1070, Schenfeld was the centre of the Saxonian Holstengau. The place was first mentioned in a charter in 1256.

name: Schependorf
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1339.

name: Schepsdorf
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1313. The name of the village is derived from the ferry (schep = 'ship') across the Ems.

name: Schermbeck
Fair_Description: Two fairs are mentioned in 1485, on Sunday after Easter and 1 November, with a duration of three days before and after. A weekly market took place on Thursday-Saturday.
Toll_Description: The Count of Cleves levied a land toll in 1362.

name: Schernikau
Settlement_Description: First mention in 1292; mention of an innkeep in 1375.

name: Mikkeli
Settlement_Description: <b>Inn:</b> An inn was established in Mikkeli parish village in 1649. Old local official Eerikki Peitsar was appointed as the innkeeper.

name: Scherpenheuvel
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1066. Next mention in 1099-1138.

name: Scheemda
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1282, in a sixteenth or seventeenth century copy.

name: Schlewecke
Settlement_Description: The village was first mentioned in 1642.

name: Karankamäki (Mäkivola)
Settlement_Description: <b>Inn:</b> Karankamäki is the traditional border between Häme and Savo regions. An inn was established nearby in Mäkivola in 1641, and Yrjö Tuomaanpoika was appointed as the innkeeper.
