Fair_Description: In 1473, it is mentioned that Sint Jansteen had the right to hold a fair on the Day of St John. The fair must have existed before, as can be inferred from toll regulations from Hulst from 1317.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Schelde near Appels is attested in an itinerary from 1346.

name: Langerbrugge
Bridge_Description: The "long bridge" north of Gent was already mentioned in 1235.

name: Kluizen
Settlement_Description: Count Boudewijn VII (1111-1119) founded the lordship ('heerlijkheid') Twaalf Hofsteden for the cultivation of moorland with 12 farms and donated it to the monastery Ename. It became known as Kluizen after the monastic farm.
Toll_Description: According to an investigation of the burgrave of Gent in 1369, a toll was levied on the bridge Burggravenbrug across the Schipgracht canal near the mill of Kluizen. The bridge is first mentioned in 1228. The toll was levied on the cargo of ships on the canal, predominantly peat.
Bridge_Description: The Burggravenbrug across the Schipgracht canal near the mill in Kluizen was first mentioned in 1228.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Oostburg was located on a sea inlet connected to the North Sea and Zwin. The harbour silted up in the 14th century. A charter from 1443 shows, that there did not exist any shipping traffic in the harbour anymore.

name: null
Lock_Description: The Treene river was dammed in 1570 to secure the land against flooding. Three sluices were built, around which later Friedrichstadt developed. A new shipping lock was built in 1588.

name: Erfde
Settlement_Description: Church village, first mentioned in ca. 1438.

name: Yersekeroord
Toll_Description: Toll on sailing transport on South-Beveland belonging to the count of Holland first mentioned in 1321. In 1410 there were outposts in Kats, Arnemuiden and Welzinge. In 1416 and 1445 an outpost was located in Arnemuiden with the aim to tax the Flemish goods coming from the west and transshipped for Walcheren, but this was hampered by Middelburg. A tariff for the Hansa is dated 1454 and edited. In 1462 new outposts are mentioned in Arnemuiden, Veere and Vlissingen. In the years 1470-'99 the toll was pawned to Middelburg. Bergen op Zoom obtained toll-exemption, including its fairs in 1372,  Brouwershaven in 1351 and Reimerswaal in 1355 for the ships incoming from Flanders and Brabant to its fairs. The toll-booth is painted on the socalled 'Scheldekaart' dated circa 1505, opposite to Bergen op Zoom as a fortified tower. In 1532 the toll was relocated to Antwerp, probably as a result of the floods of 1530. Yields for the farming out of this domain are known for the years 1346-1572 and edited. The yields of the 15th century are studied in relation to the fairs of Bergen (op Zoom). Those for the years 1500-72 are studied in relation to the economic development of Antwerp. A small range of accounts, dated 1418, 1470-75, 1506 and 1570, is preserved and edited. A specified tariff dated 1519 is preserved and edited. A list of toll exempted places dated 1555 is preserved and edited.
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Yersekeroord first appears in accounts of the count of Holland dated 1330-1333. The ferry was usually farmed out by the count. Around 1500, Bergen op Zoom is mentioned as destination harbour. A few other ferries to Bergen op Zoom belonging to Yersekeroord operated further to the south. All ferry operations ended when Yersekeroord and its surroundings drowned during floods in 1530.

name: null
Toll_Description: Income from the outpost here from the toll at Iersekeroord dated 1470-75 and 1518 and 1524/5 are edited. Accounts of the outpost of the Grote Zeeuwse tol here dated 1584-92 and 1628vv are digitalised.
Harbour_Description: The harbour of Middelburg was located at a dam in the Arne river, which might have already existed in the late 10th century. A crane is first mentioned in the oldest city-account dated 1365/6. Income from the socalled 'cancelioen- or pondgeld' levied from transshipment in the harbour are preserved and edited for the years 1404-64. It was a shared right between town and count. In 1482 Middelburg forbade almost all trade-activities in the outport of Arnemuiden (at the mouth of the Arne at the socalled 'Walchers rede'), in 1531 after a judicial sentence this was mitigated. The river gradually silted up, so that a new straight canal was built in 1535 to connect the old harbour to the sealanes of the Schelde delta. An additional harbour basin south of the old harbour was constructed around 1540. In 1545 en 1549 the extension of the harbour of Vlissingen was sucessfully averted with a sentence of king Charles V. This would have been desastrous for the harbour of Middelburg, but also those of Zierikzee, Reimerswaal en Goes. In 1559 Middelburg obtained the right of the 'gauge' of the western wines (see sub staple).

name: Venray
Fair_Description: In 1533 (July 20) the duke of Gelre granted his stadtholder at Roermond, who was a.o. lord of Oestrom, to have a fair at Oestrum or Lulle (Lull a hamlet, later called St. Antoniusveld). The account of the steward of Kessel dated 1582 mentions a toll with St. Hubertsfair (Nov. 3) and Mayfair altera Servatij (May 13) at [Ven]Raij in 1570. The toll on the 'Lulsen' fair under 'Raij' was not organised. The account of the steward of Kessel dated 1576 mentions a toll on St. Hubert and the May-fair which were leased for 6 years, this was the last year. The 'Lulsche' fair was not organised.

name: null
Ferry_Description: First mentioned in 1381 (possibly earlier in 1294). The ferry was in private ownership, split between multiple people. This ferry was moved when the Menno van Coehoorn fortress was build in 1699.

name: Katwijk
Ferry_Description: Katwijk was the destination of the ferry across the Maas near Mook (see Mooksche Veer).

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll levied from the Hansa in Arnemuiden is found in 1384-86. Statistics of the toll called 'ankerage' levied from foreign skippers are edited for the years 1431-1571 (specified for those from the Hansa dated 1538-71, for the Bretons dated 1518-71 and for the skippers of France 1518-71). In the toll-accounts of Iersekeroord dated 1470-'75 as an outpost of this toll next to Middelburg, Kats, Vlissingen and Bergen op Zoom. In 1527 it is called a toll from the emperor of which ' t Oge (Callantsoog) is exempt. Accounts of the outpost here of the Grote Zeeuwse toll dated 1584-92 and 1628vv are digitalised.
Ferry_Description: A ferry from Goes to the island Walcheren is mentioned in 1405, but an exact destination point on the island is not mentioned. Here the assumption of Horsten is followed, that this was near Arnemuiden.
Harbour_Description: The outport of Middelburg mid 16th century and the location of the famous Walcherse Rede. But Middelburg tried initial to hamper the development here in order to protect her own harbour (see sub harbour Middelburg). The silting up of the river Arne made this on the long run impossible. In 1500 Arnemuiden already asked permission of Middelburg to deepen her harbour.

name: null
Toll_Description: Income from the outpost here from the toll at Iersekeroord dated 1418, 1470-74 and 1524/5 are edited. Accounts of the outpost here of the Grote Zeeuwse toll dated 1584-92 and 1628vv are digitalised.

name: null
Toll_Description: Although Lübeck was exempted by the bishop of Ratzeburg and the lord of Mecklenburg from the bridge toll in 1219-1220, this was probably not the case for all travellers. At least between 1643 and 1790, a toll was levied at the bridge and boom barrier of Dassow.
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Stepenitz is mentioned in 1219, when the bishop of Ratzeburg relinquished his toll right on the bridge in favour of Lübeck. The next year Nikolaus II of Mecklenburg did the same. The bridge might have existed since the early 13th century or even earlier. The wooden bridge often had to be repaired, for which Lübeck and Mecklenburg paid the costs.
Harbour_Description: The bridge was also used as a loading place for ships. These could reach the Baltic Sea via the Dassower See and Trave.

name: Haastrechtse brug
Bridge_Description: Relocation towards Gouda of the bridge near Haastrecht built in 1467.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge crossing the Hollandse IJssel built in 1467, was relocated towards Gouda in 1471.
Ferry_Description: A ferry to the Land van Stein (part of the parish of Haastrecht) at the opposite bank of the Hollandse IJssel is first mentioned in 1299.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge over the Hollandse IJssel is first mentioned in 1329.
Ferry_Description: A ferry in the adjacent village Eiteren at the Hollandse IJssel is first mentioned in 1277: ‘navim meam de Eytere, que vulgo verscep dicitur’. In 1310 the parish Eiteren was combined with IJsselstein.

name: Gemert
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1076-1081, in a (possibly falsified) 12th-century copy.

name: Hilvarenbeek
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1155, in a 13th-century copy.
Fair_Description: Hilvarenbeek had a fair in 1370-'80, which afterwards perished but revived again between 1524-'55.

name: Pannerden
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1052-1056, in an 11th-century copy.

name: Het Hemeltje
Settlement_Description: The farm 't Hemeltje probably dates back to the 16th century and is first mentioned indirectly in 1625 in the names of the farmers Jan and Jasper Hemmelkenbelt. It was located on the old post road between Holten and Bathmen. An inn only appears in the late 18th century, and was located on the "new farm" northeast of the old farm.

name: Tielen
Settlement_Description: The castle Tileburg was built by the count of Holstein as defence against Dithmarschen around 1300. It is first mentioned in 1323 and became the administrative centre of a regional district ('Amt'). It was located at the confluence of the Tielenau with the Eider river, slightly upstream from the current location of Tielen. On the northern side of the river, the village Tielen was located, first mentioned in 1423. The castle was destroyed by Dithmarschen in 1500 and not rebuilt. In 1533, Tielen was relocated to its current position, where the hamlet Hude was located before.
Toll_Description: A toll station at the Tileburg castle on the Eider river of the counts of Holstein is first mentioned in 1341. In 1345, it is mentioned that it was first levied by count Heinrich, probably the builder of the castle, who died in 1304. After the partition of Schleswig and Holstein in a royal and a ducal part in 1490, the toll came to the duke. First mentions of a toll tariff dates from 1506, first detailed regulations from 1519. The toll station was moved to Süderstapel in 1594.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Treene in Schwabstedt is first mentioned around 1460. During the 15th and 16th centuries a duty from the ferry across Treene was paid to Schwabstedt Castle.

name: Usedom
Settlement_Description: The "urbs" Osna, a Slavic fortification, was destroyed by the Danes in 1115-1119. The first mention dates back to 1128, when a local council was held in Usedom. The first reference in a charter dates from 14-10-1140, which specified the ownership of Usedom Castle.
Town_Description: Next to the castle a market settlement developed. It is first mentioned as small town or borough ('oppidum') in 1267. Acquisition of Lübeck town privileges from Duke Bogislaw IV in 1298, confirmed multiple times in the 14th century.
Toll_Description: Even before 1140, in addition to revenues from the market and inn, a ship toll ('Schiffszoll') held by the Slavic sovereignty existed. From 1140, the bishopric was involved. However, the toll was soon devalued (ca. 1230s) and a fixed rent ('Rente') was introduced in 1240.

name: Jarmen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1269. Originally probably a Slavic fishing village.
Town_Description: A planned town was founded around 1250, first mentioned as borough ('opidum') in 1290. Later it had Lübeck town privileges, the year of acquisition is unknown.

name: Lassan
Settlement_Description: Slavic settlement and castle around 1000, first mentioned in 1136. A parish church is mentioned in 1248.
Town_Description: Acquisition of town privileges probably around 1270. First mentioned as 'civitas' in 1291.

name: null
Toll_Description: A river toll in Havelberg is first mentioned in 1259. In 1570 or 1580 the episcopal toll on the Havel is moved from Nitzow to Havelberg.

name: Penkun
Settlement_Description: Originated as a castle, first mentioned in 1240.
Town_Description: Characterised as 'opidum' in 1269 and as 'civitas' in 1284. The Magdeburg town rights are mentioned in 1285.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Heiligenhafen was founded as harbour town for eastern Holstein and received harbour privileges in 1350. The harbour was mainly important for corn exports from Holstein to the Danish islands and the German harbour towns. The old harbour was probably located at the end of the Brückstraße, named after a landing pier.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The harbour for traffic on the Treene river was located on the western side of town.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The Süderbootfahrt canal, dug in 1613, connected Garding with the Eider river and North Sea via a lock in Kating.

name: Katingsiel
Lock_Description: A sluice near Kating connected the canal Süderbootfahrt, dug in 1613, with the Eider river and the North Sea.

name: Süderzollhaus
Settlement_Description: Originally a manor called Lütken Kragstede, that had been abandoned for a long time in 1596. In that year, a toll house was built here. An inn was built in 1608.
Toll_Description: Toll station of the district of Flensburg, installed in 1596 when the road between Flensburg and Husum was renewed.

name: Lunden
Town_Description: Town privileges were granted in 1529. After the conquest of Dithmarschen in 1559, they were repealed. Lunden remained capital of the northern part of Dithmarschen.
Fair_Description: In Heinrich Rantzau's description of Schleswig and Holstein from 1597, two fairs are mentioned on Palm Sunday and St Michael's Day. These are also mentioned in an almanac printed in Neudamm (Dębno) in 1598.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Wismar was an important harbour town from its very beginning, the harbour is first mentioned in 1211. Ships from the town were active in international seafaring to Scandinavia, England and the Baltic Sea.

name: Echten (Drente)
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1181, in a 15th-century copy.

name: Kilen
Ferry_Description: The age and character of the ferry across the narrow strait of Kilen is uncertain. The ferry was first mentioned in 1578, but is most likely significantly older. In the early modern era the responsibility of the ferry was in the hands of the steward (Danish: lensmand) of Ørum. In the period 1589 to 1640 the ferry was replaced by a bridge. When the bridge collapsed in 1640, the ferry connection was reestablished.

name: Gedstedbro
Toll_Description: In 1570 a royal toll station was built at Gedsted to collect toll on transportation of oxen across the bridge.
Bridge_Description: The exact age of the bridge across the river of Lerkenfeld Å is unknown. As part of the prehistoric route system of Hærvejen/Ochsenweg through Jutland a bridge was built in the early middle ages or before. The bridge is, however, not mentioned before 1464.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge crossing the Hollandse IJssel was granted by duke Albrecht on 1 May 1371.
Ferry_Description: A ferry ('veerscepe') is first mentioned in 1334 in the account of the count of Holland. It dit not replace the bridge as it is still found in 1443.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Due to its location where the end of a fjord reached the main north-south route through the Jutland peninsula, Flensburg became an important harbour town. Quay structures ('schiffsbrücke') are first mentioned in 1480.

name: Sundstrup Færge
Ferry_Description: Ferry across the narrow strait of Virksund near the inlet to Hjarbæk Fjord. According to a document from 1452 the ferry belonged to the diocese in Viborg, and this has also been the case in the past. The exact age and character of the ferry is, however, uncertain. Presumably the ferry existed early in the medieval period. In 1514 a certain Niels Clementsen was granted the right to the ferry for the rest of his life.

name: Slepeldamme
Settlement_Description: The settlement originated around a lock in the Ee river, which was first mentioned in 1244. The village had some significance as fish market. The area flooded in 1583 during wartime inundations and the settlement was not rebuilt afterwards.
Toll_Description: Slepeldamme was one of the stations where the toll on the Zwin of the counts of Flanders was levied. It is first mentioned as such in 1368, but probably installed shortly after 1252. In a toll-account dated 1328/'9 found as an outpost of Damme.
Lock_Description: A lock that closed off the Ee river to Aardenburg from the sea is first mentioned in 1244 and must have been built shortly before. Since Aardenburg lost its economic significance in the 14th century, the lock was often in a dilapidated state. It was destroyed in 1583 during wartime inundations.

name: Middelburg (Vlaanderen)
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1404. The settlement was property of the abbey of Middelburg in Zeeland, from which it derived its name.

name: Foldingbro
Toll_Description: From 1521 onwards the local peasants had to pay a fee (Danish: brokorn/bropenge) to cross the bridge. A new royal roll station and toll on oxen was introduced in 1570. But the toll on oxen, and most likely also other commodities, was probably also collected earlier in the later middle ages.
Bridge_Description: The exact age and character of the bridge across the river of Kongeå is unknown. As Folding was central part of the prehistoric route system of Hærvejen/Ochsenweg through Jutland a bridge was built in the early middle ages. The place name of "Foldingbro" is a reference to a bridge. The bridge is, however, not documented before the early 16th century. An inn at Foldingbro was mentioned for the first time in 1521. At this time the steward (Danish: lensmand) at Tørning castle was responsible for maintaining the bridge.

name: Hagebro
Toll_Description: A toll on using the bridge was first mentioned in the first half of the 16th century, but is without any doubts much older. In 1523 the income of the toll from the bridge belonged to the monastery of Stubber, which also had to maintain the bridge. A few years later, during the 1520ties, the king handed over the income from the bridge to the nobleman Ejler Bryske. In 1549 the bridge was in a bad condition, and therefore the king granted the nobleman Iver Juel the income of the bridge. In return Iver Juel had to maintain the bridge.
Bridge_Description: One of the most important crossings of the large river of Karup Å. The exact age of the bridge is unknown, but probably built in the early middle ages. The place name of Hagebro is an explicit reference to a bridge at this locality. The bridge was, however, not mentioned before 1523. In 1549 the bridge needed to be repaired.

name: Bækmarksbro
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge is uncertain. Probably from the later medieval period.

name: Håls
Bridge_Description: The age of the bridge is uncertain. Probably more or less contemporary with Løvel Bridge. The stone bridge went across the river of Lindenborg Å.

name: Rindelev
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge across the river of Ringkloster Å is uncertain. In the late medieval period and early modern era the bridge played a central role in the export of oxen in this part of Jutland.

name: Skærum Bro
Toll_Description: A fee was paid to cross the bridge (Danish: bropenge/brokorn). The income apparently belonged to the manor of Nørre Vosborg.
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge across Storå is uncertain. Probably from the late medieval period. The income from the bridge belonged to owners of the nearby manor of Nørre Vosborg.

name: Bering Bro
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge across the river of Aarhus Å is uncertain. In the late medieval period and early modern era the bridge played a role in the export of oxen in this part of Jutland.

name: Lisbjerg Bro
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge across the river of Egå is uncertain. In the late medieval period and early modern era the bridge was used by travelers between the towns of Randers and Aarhus. The bridge played a central role in the export of oxen in this part of Jutland.

name: null
Ferry_Description: Schwedt was located on an old crossing of the Oder river. A ferry is mentioned in 1563.
Harbour_Description: Schwedt was a transshipment point between shipping on the Oder and land traffic, among others for citizens from Angermünde, who were exempted from toll payments in 1350.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bishop of Utrecht granted permission to build a wooden bridge across the IJssel near Deventer on 26 August 1482. It was opened for traffic on 16 March 1483. The bridge was destroyed multiple times: by troops from Guelders in 1522 (rebuilt in 1539), by ice in 1570 (rebuilt in 1576), and once again by troops from Guelders in 1578. A new bridge was only constructed around 1600 as pontoon bridge further upstream.
Ferry_Description: Before the construction of the bridge in 1482, a ferry crossing existed here. It also operated later when the bridge was destroyed and not yet rebuilt: in 1522-1539, 1570-1576 and 1578-1600.

name: Grimnitz
Settlement_Description: Castle of the Ascanians, first mentioned in 1297. The dilapidated castle was converted into a hunting lodge for the Elector of Brandenburg in the 16th century.

name: null
Bridge_Description: Bridge across the canal between Brussels and Willebroek, built between 1550 and 1561.

name: null
Toll_Description: In order to enforce the Mechelen staple and toll privileges on the Zenne river, the river could be closed with a chain in Heffen.

name: Nieuwerhaven
Settlement_Description: The settlement Ten Oerde is first mentioned in 1303. In 1441-1442, a new harbour for drainage purposes was constructed here for the settlement Groede, after which the place became known as Nieuwerhaven ('new harbour'). The settlement was inundated during the Dutch Revolt in 1583 and never rebuilt.
Toll_Description: In 1502, it is mentioned that the toll formerly levied in Hugevliet was levied since 7 or 8 years in Nieuwerhaven. The toll was subsequently abolished because of the construction of the canal Brugse Vaart south of Oostburg.
Ferry_Description: Ten Oerde is mentioned in 1303 as crossing place of the Westerschelde to the island Walcheren. It must be identical with the place Ter Ouder Vere ('at the old ferry') known from other sources. This was the landing place of the ferry between Vlissingen and Flanders until 1583, when the place was inundated. The ferry must have moved to Breskens afterwards.
Harbour_Description: Nieuwerhaven was built as a harbour for the settlement Groede in 1441-1442. Although mainly for drainage of the countryside, at least around 1500 it is also mentioned that transshipment took place here, because the harbour of Sluis was difficult to reach.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Oldemarkt had access to navigable waterways via the Mallegat and Linde to Kuinre.

name: null
Harbour_Description: In 1349 Greifenhagen received the privilege of shipping on the Regelitz, Dammscher See, Swinestrom and Peene, thereby circumventing the staple of Stettin (Szczecin).

name: null
Harbour_Description: Oderberg was a transshipment point between the land traffic and shipping on the Oder river.

name: null
Toll_Description: Veere obtained toll-exemption in Holland and Zeeland in 1341. The earliest mention of a toll on herring is dated 1399. Toll-accounts are preserved for the years 1477-'81 and 1486. The oldest one is analysed. In 1462 the king of England granted free shipment. In 1465 the king of France gave privileges for trade, in particular to Bordeaux and La Rochelle for trade in salt. In 1472 the lord of Veere granted toll-exemption to the subjects of the king of England. In the toll-accounts of Iersekeroord dated 1470-'75 Veere is an outpost of this toll next to Middelburg, Arnemuiden, Kats, Vlissingen and Bergen op Zoom. In 1527 it is called a toll from the emperor of which ' t Oge (Callantsoog) is exempt. Accounts of the outpost here of the Grote Zeeuwse toll dated 1584-92 and 1628vv are digitalised.
Ferry_Description: The existence of a ferry to Kampen (Noord-Beveland) is attested by the original name Campvere for the town, first mentioned in 1282. Ferry services stopped when Noord-Beveland was flooded in 1532, but were started again after parts of the island were reclaimed from the sea in the 17th century.
Harbour_Description: In 1282 the lord of the town and his wife donated all their property which they had bought from count Floris V, including a harbour, harbour-dike and harbour-taxes, to his wife countess Beatrix, who gave it back in fief. The harbour was dug in an old creek on initiative of the lord of the town around 1280. In 1490 a 'kaaigeld' (quay-tax) or 'wintersate' (place for the ships to hibernate) was installed. This was property of the lord of the town who donated the rights in 1553 to the town. In 1541 Veere became the stapleplace for the Scots, because here was less competition of the Merchant Adventurers. In 1578 the staple was reinstalled after it had disappeared for some years. On the map of Jacob van Deventer the town is still within its old walls. The entrance to the harbour is protected with two towers and is also within the walls. Outside the town is a 'Molenwater', which served as a sluice to deepen te harbour with the help of a watermill. Ships from Domburg harboured in Veere. In 1560 at the north-side of the harbour a navy-arsenal was built. Circa 1560 there were 55 ships to catch fish (circa 1600 54)), in 1570 14 herringbusses. Veere was the centre of the socalled 'botvaarders', who catched flat-fish before the coast of Flanders. Around 1600 the Kille was enlarged and joined with the 'spuiwater' (Molenwater), which enlarged the harbour. From Veere it was like Vlissingen five quarters of an hour's to Middelburg.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Harbour on the Alster river. In 1618, the Lübeck city council was informed that one should use the waterway between Bergstedt and Poppenbüttel or Fuhlsbüttel on the way to Hamburg, because of closure of the Steindamm street.

name: null
Bridge_Description: Bridge across the canal between Brussels and Willebroek, built between 1550 and 1561.

name: null
Bridge_Description: First mentioned in 1353, when the burgrave who levied toll illegally was ordained by the bishop of Utrecht to tear down the existing bridge and built a new one that could be passed freely by ships. A bridge must therefore have already existed before 1353.
Ferry_Description: A ferry is first mentioned in 1282. It must have been replaced by a bridge before 1353.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll was levied by the town of Frankfurt to finance the construction and maintenance of the bridge.
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Oder is already mentioned in the town privileges from 1253.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Already in 1298, Fürstenwalde is mentioned as transshipment point between river transport on the Spree to Berlin and the land route to Frankfurt.

name: null
Toll_Description: Because of the opening of the new street Frankfurt-Crossen in 1535, Frankfurt received the right to levy a toll at the bridge and dam at the mill in Reipzig to finance its maintenance. The toll was calculated according to the number of horses and vehicles.
Bridge_Description: Bridge and dam across the Eilang at the water mill of Reipzig. With the opening of the new street between Frankfurt and Crossen in 1535, the bridge and dam were renewed to accommodate the heaver traffic.

name: Urad Górny
Bridge_Description: Bridge across the Pleiske (Pliszka) near Aurith (Urad).

name: null
Ferry_Description: Ferries to Walcheren, Noord-Beveland, Duiveland en Schouwen are mentioned in 1405; In 1449 to Antwerp, Walcheren, Zierikzee and Sluis. In 1492 the latter is not mentioned anymore. Market-boats ('beurtveren') are then mentioned to Steenbergen and Dordrecht.

name: Egmond-Binnen
Settlement_Description: The oldest abbey in the Netherlands was founded by count Dirk II around 950. A hospital was first mentioned in 1239. In the late Middle Ages the addition "Binnen" to the name appears to discern the settlement from nearby Egmond aan den Hoef and Egmond aan Zee. The abbey was destroyed in 1573, in order to prevent providing a refuge for the advancing Spanish army.

name: Frankfurter Niederlage
Harbour_Description: When the Spree river was made navigable upstream from Fürstenwalde by the construction of a lock there in 1588, the town of Frankfurt installed a harbour with warehouse at the lake Kersdorfer See as transshipment place to the Frankfurt staple.

name: null
Toll_Description: Because of the opening of the street Frankfurt-Crossen via Ziebingen for commercial traffic in 1535, the toll of Reppen was moved before the long Oder bridge in Frankfurt.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry in Katendrecht is first mentioned in 1323.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The transshipment point between the land traffic and the shipping on the Oder river was moved from Niederfinow to Eberswalde in 1317.

name: null
Bridge_Description: In 1542 Niederfinow is referred to as bridge town at the Finow. Before, in 1317, the main Finow crossing had been moved from here to Eberswalde.
Harbour_Description: In 1308 a place of transshipment from the river to land transport is established in Niederfinow. In 1317, the transshipment place is moved to Eberswalde. Commodities unloaded in Niederfinow now had to be brought to Eberswalde first.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Wriezen was predominantly important as fish market for the surrounding villages.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Havel in Henningsdorf was constructed in 1672.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Guben was an important place of transshipment between the land transport and shipping on the Neiße and Oder rivers. The first mention of shipping in Guben dates from 1211 when Duke Henry I granted Lebus monastery toll-free passage on the Oder to Guben.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Elbe in Dresden was built in 1271, but destroyed by floods in 1275. A stone bridge is mentioned in 1287, which was once again destroyed in 1342 and later rebuilt.

name: veer
Ferry_Description: A comital ferry crossing the Krommenie is first mentioned in 1325.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge crossing the river Amstel is first mentioned in 1339. Precise location uncertain.

name: null
Toll_Description: The accounts of the comital steward of West-Friesland mention from 1383 onwards combined revenues of: 'gancael en sciptol' (in 1396: 'ghanc van onse aeltienden' or thithes of the eel and a toll on ships) and combined revenues of harbour and castle ('slot').
Ferry_Description: A market-boat ('beurtveer') to Amsterdam is first mentioned in 1550.
Harbour_Description: The medieval harbour was a small canal through the town with a north-south course, which was built over in 1542 (or 44?) for an extension of the market place. Around 1400 an outer harbour came into being, among others to accommodate larger ships. A new harbour ('Nieuwe Haven') was built south of the old town in 1544, and later became known as old harbour ('Oude Haven'). In 1549 emperor Charles granted the magistrate to levy a 'lastgeld' (3 rijnsguilders per last) from the hibernating ships in the new harbour, in order to maintain the harbour. Vitelli counted in his report for the duke of Alva in 1569 60 'buizen' (herringboats), 30 boats, 180 'binnenlanders' (ships for inland trade) and 350 ships with 'gabes': crow's-nest) with destinations Zierikzee and England.The Opstand against Spain caused the relocation of Waterland skippers from the mouth of Meuse to Enkhuizen. There they left via the Marsdiep. Around 1577 some 140 herringboats were harboured here, in 1625 270 and in 1654 246 who caught herring near Great Yarmouth.  Between 1630-35 new harbours were made (Nieuwe Haven and the Oude and the Nieuwe or St. Pieters Buishaven for hibernating herringboats).

name: brug Gein
Bridge_Description: In 1388 the Gein bridge is found opposite of the Hofland in the ambacht (manor) Weesp.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Alblas is first found in 1331 in the oldest account of the steward of the count of Zuidholland.

name: Almsvoet
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1105. The settlement was submerged during the Flood of St Elisabeth of 1421.
Toll_Description: Toll belonging to the count of Holland on the river Alm, first mentioned in 1250, in 1274 mentioned as Dubbelmonde. Submerged in 1421/1424 by the floods of St Elisabeth. Relocated to Geertruidenberg but not succesfully.

name: null
Ferry_Description: Ferry to the toll house Almsvoet belonging to the count of Holland, first mentioned in 1331. Submerged in 1421 by the Flood of St Elisabeth.

name: Feldheim
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned around 1400.

name: Wattenscheid
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as dispersed settlement ('bauerschaft') in the 9th century; a church is first mentioned in 1147.
Town_Description: Town-like ('wigbold') privileges granted by Count Adolf of the Mark between 1413 and 1417, and by his brother Gerhard in 1432. The settlement was mostly mentioned as "Freiheit", sometimes as "Stadt" (town).
Fair_Description: A weekly market on Friday was granted by Count Gerhard of Cleves in 1432, although the original borough ('wigbold') privileges between 1413 and 1417 already mention a market day. In the town statutes of 1581, annual fairs are mentioned, although their number and dates are not specified. In a confirmation of the privileges by Margrave Friedrich Wilhelm from 1661-1689, a third fair is granted on the day of the Visitation (2 July) and the day before.

name: null
Ferry_Description: In 1347, a ferry is mentioned to Zierikzee, in 1355 to Antwerp and in 1408 to Bruges. A market-boat ('beurtveer') to Amsterdam is first mentioned in 1539.

name: veer Yppensloot
Ferry_Description: Ferry from Yppensloot (later: Nieuwen Diep) to Waterland. First mentioned in 1308 in the oldest account of the bailliff of Amstelland of the count of Holland.

name: null
Toll_Description: A bridge toll and fee for safe conduct is mentioned in 1367, when it was moved to Cottbus. However, in 1653 and 1673, a bridge and transit toll in Fehrow is still attested.
Bridge_Description: In 1357, Margrave Louis the Roman granted permission to Lord John of Cottbus to build a bridge and dam across the Spree river at Fehrow.
Ferry_Description: The name Fehrow is derived from a ferry across the Spree river, which was replaced by a bridge in 1357.

name: Jasień
Town_Description: Town privileges granted by Duke Christian of Saxony-Merseburg in 1660.

name: Borne (Bad Belzig)
Settlement_Description: The church village is first mentioned in 1227.

name: Wiesenburg
Settlement_Description: A castle districh ('Burgward') is first mentioned in 1162. Next to the castle a settlement developed, which was referred to as small town ('Städtlein') since 1443.

name: Zschackau
Settlement_Description: The village of Zschackau is first mentioned as parish in 1250. In 1938 the village was merged with Zeckritz under the name Beilrode.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry at Tangermünde is first attested in 1376. On a 17th-century view of town by Matthias Merian, the ferry landing place is located directly at the Elbe riverfront on the peninsula in front of the town.

name: Krevese
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 956.

name: Friedland (Niederlausitz)
Settlement_Description: The church of Friedland is mentioned in 1346.
Town_Description: Was a town before the 30 Years' War.

name: Storkow
Settlement_Description: Around 1200, there existed a German castle next to a Slavic fishing village and a market village. First mentioned in 1209.
Town_Description: Nothing is known about the foundation of the town. Characterised as town since 1450, from the 16th century only small town ('Städtchen').

name: Groitzsch
Settlement_Description: A castle was founded next to a Slavic settlement in the 10th century and first mentioned in c. 1073.
Town_Description: A planned town was founded around 1200. It received market and toll privileges in 1219. The town privileges were confirmed in 1429.
Toll_Description: The town received toll privileges in 1219.

name: Königs Wusterhausen
Settlement_Description: Castle of Brandenburg, first mentioned in 1320, with a Slavic settlement. A mill is mentioned in 1366. The settlement only became a borough ('Flecken') in the 18th century, and acquired town rights in 1935.
Toll_Description: The lords ('Schenken') of Landsberg, who resided on castle Teupitz, owned the land toll in Teupitz, as well as the bridge and dam tolls in Königs Wusterhausen and Märkisch Buchholz.

name: null
Toll_Description: The Elbe toll in Mühlberg only entered the possession of the electorate in Sachsen at the end of the 15th century. A registry of safe conduct from 1555 merely lists the toll due on mill-, cut-, and limestones, as well as grain. Wood is only mentioned indirectly in the fee for rafts. The toll is also mentioned in the 17th century.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The Elbe ferry at Merschwitz is mentioned in a statement of three wagoners from 1483.

name: null
Toll_Description: The city council levied a toll on the bridge of 4 Heller for each wagon. The tariffs were raised in 1436 to 1 old Groschen for each wagon, 2 Groschen for each rider, 1 Heller for each pedestrian.
Bridge_Description: The Elbe bridge in Meißen is first attested in 1291. It is mentioned in possession of the town council in 1316.

name: Schafbrücke
Bridge_Description: In the Thirty Year's War the toll bridge at Ammersdorf is destroyed and replaced by a wooden construction in 1653. In 1733 it is replaced again by a stone bridge that is preserved until today.

name: Nieuwersluis
Lock_Description: Circa 1466 a lock was made here at the river Vecht for small boats connecting Utrecht and Amsterdam via the Angstel and Amstel rivers. Previously trans-shipment was necessary at the Botterdam near Ter Aa. In 1527 Utrecht promised the emperor to make a new lock with two good doors, where at most 13x in 24 hours ships would be handled. This in order to prevent waterflooding from the river Vecht on to Amstelland, what had caused disagreements for a long time.

name: Werdau
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in 1304, when it was already a town, but it probably originated in the second half of the 12th century as a farming village with a market in possession of the lords of Crimmitschau.
Town_Description: The settlement was elevated into a town and fortified between 1260 and 1300. First mentioned as 'civitas' in 1304. Councillors are first mentioned in 1397. The town privileges were derived from those of Zwickau and confirmed in 1398.

name: null
Toll_Description: Station of secondary safe conduct of Chemnitz

name: Wilsdruff
Settlement_Description: Farming village with seat of a lord, first mentioned in 1259.
Town_Description: Founded as a town in the 13th century. Called oppidum in 1281 and civitas in 1294.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Oder in Freienwalde appears in a charter from 1465.
Harbour_Description: A transshipment point for citizens from Berlin-Cölln between shipping on the Oder and land traffic in Freienwalde appears in a charter from 1409.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry near Westervoort is first mentioned in an account of the count of Guelders of 1294/95. It is unclear whether it concerns a market ferry or a ferry for passengers. The ferry of Westervoort/IJsseloord thus probably dates from the thirteenth century or earlier. In 1765, it was replaced by a pontoon bridge.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll in Loitz is first mentioned in 1267, when Greifswald was exempted. In an exemption for the monastery Dargun from 1275, the toll is specified as bridge and water toll. A new toll was installed by Bogislaw X in 1480.
Bridge_Description: The mention of a bridge toll in 1275 is the first evidence for the existence of a bridge in Loitz. From a view of town by Merian from 1652 and 17th-century accounts it is clear that it was a single draw bridge. The bridge was destroyed in the Brandenburg-Swedish war of 1675-1680 and rebuilt in 1681.

name: null
Toll_Description: In 1570 or 1580 the episcopal toll on the Havel is moved from Nitzow to Havelberg.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Königsberg acquired the right of toll-free shipping on the Oder and Rurzyca rivers towards Stettin. The privilege was renewed in 1354.

name: Garz (Rügen)
Settlement_Description: The settlement originated in the close proximity of a Wendish rampart and was named in 1157 as a result of the invasion of the Danes. It was first mentioned in a document in 1232.
Town_Description: The year of acquisition of town rights is unknown. Town councillors are first mentioned in 1319. The town had the Schwerin town law.

name: null
Toll_Description: Already in 1254, Stettin acquired the ferry toll on the road between the town and Altdamm. After the construction of a causeway and bridges between the two towns after 1299, the toll was levied on the road. The view of Stettin by Braun and Hogeberg (16th century) displays a toll house on the bridge across the Regelitz.
Bridge_Description: A causeway between Stettin and Altdamm with bridges across the arms of the Oder was built after 1299 by Stettin with support of Duke Otto of Pomerania, who supplied building material.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A causeway between Stettin and Altdamm with bridges across the arms of the Oder was built after 1299 by Stettin with support of Duke Otto of Pomerania, who supplied building material.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A causeway between Stettin and Altdamm with bridges across the arms of the Oder was built after 1299 by Stettin with support of Duke Otto of Pomerania, who supplied building material.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A causeway between Stettin and Altdamm with bridges across the arms of the Oder was built after 1299 by Stettin with support of Duke Otto of Pomerania, who supplied building material.

name: Anklamer Fähre
Settlement_Description: The island called Fähre ('ferry') was first mentioned in 1285 when Bogislaw gave it in fief to his vassals, two Anklam townsmen. Before that, the island was probably owned by the knight Johann von Berlin. It is unclear if there originally existed a ferry at this place.
Toll_Description: The town of Anklam acquired the right to levy a toll on the island Fähre in 1302.

name: Bergen auf Rügen
Settlement_Description: A Cistercian Women's monastery was founded by Lord Jaromar I of Rügen in 1193. Around the monastery the market borough ('flecken') Bergen developed in the 13th century, first mentioned in 1232.
Town_Description: Acquisition of Lübeck town privileges in 1613.
Fair_Description: A fair on Palm Sunday in Bergen is mentioned in an almanac printed in Neudamm (Dębno) in 1598.

name: Altefähr
Settlement_Description: The village served as a ferry dock as early as the 13th century. In 1294, the parish of "Vere" was mentioned for the first time.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry to Altefähr ('old ferry') probably already existed in the 13th century.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry probably already existed in the 13th century.

name: Werder (Havel)
Settlement_Description: Originally a Slavic settlement and fortification on an island in the Havel river. First mentioned in 1317 as borough ('oppidum'), usually called little town ('städtlein'), but only became a town in 1809.

name: Nowe Warpno
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1352 as town. The settlement Werpene first mentioned in 1184 might also refer to Altwarp. The first mention of the addition "antiqua Warpe" in 1313 suggest that a "new" Warp also existed at that time.
Town_Description: First mentioned in 1352 as "civitas Nova Warpe", although the town might have been founded before 1295. Town privileges were confirmed by Duke Joachim of Pomerania in 1442. Magdeburg town law with some elements of Lübeck town law since 1556.

name: null
Harbour_Description: A harbour is mentioned in 1297. Świnoujście became an important transshipment point for shipping between the Baltic Sea and the Stettin Lagoon and Oder river, as is indicated in a privilege from 1309.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ducal ferry across the Świna river is first mentioned in 1230.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ducal ferry across the Świna at Świnoujście is first mentioned in 1230.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Duke Bogislaw IV granted free seagoing shipping and trade in 1308.

name: Sundsøre
Ferry_Description: The age and character of the ferry connection between Hvalpsund in the region of Himmerland and Sundsøre on the peninsula of Salling is uncertain. But a ferry probably existed in the 15th century, perhaps earlier. The ferry connection is, however, first documented in 1523.

name: Hohe Brücke
Bridge_Description: The "high bridge" ('hoghe Brügg') across the Recknitz between Ribnitz and Damgarten was first mentioned in 1286, when it was bought by the town Ribnitz. As one of the few passages across the marshy Recknitz valley, it was often heavily contested in the following centuries. A drawing from 1615 shows the bridge as wooden draw bridge.

name: null
Toll_Description: Merchants from Frankfurt complained in 1549 about the toll in Grimnitz.

name: null
Toll_Description: A bridge toll in Templin is first mentioned in 1320.

name: Mühlendamm
Bridge_Description: A mill weir that also functioned as bridge is first mentioned in 1309. It was located on both sides of the cathedral island and provided an obstacle for ships.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A mill weir that also functioned as bridge is first mentioned in 1309. It was located on both sides of the cathedral island and provided an obstacle for ships.

name: null
Lock_Description: The Margrave of Brandenburg allowed the citizens of Spandau to build a flash lock ('Flutrinne'), probably to circumvent the margravial water mill (first mentioned 1258) at the site of the current lock in Spandau. This first lock was probably built at another location, possibly at the canal between the old town and the suburb Behnitz. It was replaced by a new pound lock at the current location after 1556.

name: Pritzerbe
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 948. Fortification from Slavic times, a civic settlement developed around 1200. Mentioned as borough ('oppidum') in 1225, usually characterised as borough or little town. Only became a town in 1809.

name: Babelsberg
Settlement_Description: Slavic village where Germans settled in the 13th century. First mentioned in 1375. Raised into the town Nowawes in 1924, renamed into Babelsberg in 1938.

name: Schöneberg
Settlement_Description: Village founded in the third quarter of the 13th century, first mentioned in 1264. Became a town in 1898.

name: Trzemeszno Lubuskie
Settlement_Description: Village, raised into a town by the King of Prussia in 1804.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Warta in Landsberg (Gorzów Wielkopolski) is first mentioned in 1385.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on the Oder river traffic is mentioned in a charter for Driesen (Drezdenko) from 1347

name: null
Toll_Description: Landsberg (Gorzów Wielkopolski) acquired in 1316 the right to levy a dam toll; probably, this referred to the dam that crossed the southern river marsh between the town and Dechsel (Deszczno).

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on river traffic on the Noteć is mentioned in a charter for Driesen (Drezdenko) from 1347.
Bridge_Description: Elector Frederick II ordered the construction of a bridge across the Noteć in 1446, referring to the existence of an older bridge, for which there is no evidence. In 1501, the bridge had been demolished and attempts to rebuild the bridge by the owner of Santok castle Georg Rülicke met with resistance from Landsberg (Gorzów Wielkopolski), who feared circumference of the town.
Ferry_Description: Old crossing of the Noteć river; a ford is mentioned in 1269. Ferry services were prohibited here in 1539.

name: Kongensbro
Bridge_Description: The age and character of the bridge is uncertain. First mentioned in the 16th century, but probably older. In 1683 the king granted a local nobleman the right to establish an inn at the bridge.

name: Hvidøre
Settlement_Description: An inn in the 16th century. Documented in 1535, 1556 and 1568.

name: null
Harbour_Description: According to a charter from 1347, Driesen (Drezdenko) enjoyed shipping privileges on the Noteć and Warta rivers, with exemptions from toll payments on these rivers.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The town Friedeberg (Strzelce Krajeńskie) acquired the right of shipping to Stettin (Szczecin) in 1345, via the Polka (Pełcz), Noteć, Warta and Oder rivers. A transshipment point must therefore have been located on the Pełcz, probably in Altenfließ (Przyłęg).

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry (veerschip) at Stocheym is first found in 1383. It was a fief of the lord of Valkenburg. Possibly this refers to the ferry to Berg aan de Maas.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on the Meuse is first found in 983.

name: Gottskär
Town_Description: First mentioned as a town in 1481, so town privileges were granted earlier, probably around the middle of the 15th century.  In 1539 king Christian III (1534-1559) withdrew the town rights, and that the inhabitants of Gottskär had to move to Varberg.

name: Varberg
Settlement_Description: The castle of Varberg was built by count Jokob of Halland in the late 13th century, but later the castle went to the king. When the castle was built the urban settlement of Aranäs was located in the region, but this settlement disappeared, and a new urban settlement developed in the shadow of the castle. This new settlement was known under two names: Getakärr and Varberg (later Gamla Varberg).
Town_Description: In the early 14th century Varberg was counted among the towns of Denmark. Citizens of Varberg were mentioned first in 1309, and in 1343 Getakärr/Gammel Varberg was characterized as a town. Mayors and a town council are known from the early 15th century onwards. Around 1430 a new town, Ny Varberg (New Varberg), was founded at the main road running along the coast of Halland. Up until 1578 when Gammel Varberg lost its town privileges, the two towns existed side by side. A Carmelite monastery was founded in Ny Varberg in 1462. During the Kalmar War between Denmark and Sweden 1611-1613 Ny Varberg was heavily damaged, and after the war the town was rebuilt at a new location. This project was unsuccessful, and therefore the town was moved once again to its current location at Varberg castle.

name: Abbenbroek
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1206. A chapter in the church is known for the years 1483-ca. 1572.
Ferry_Description: A ferry to Geervliet is first mentioned in 1379.
Harbour_Description: In 1356 it received toll-exemption from the count of Holland.

name: Hoornse Hoofden
Ferry_Description: The ferry at Oudenhoorn was an important crossing point of the Haringvliet before it was moved to Hellevoetsluis in c. 1595. Separate ferry services existed with Sommelsdijk and Dirksland, in 1581 one ferryman operated services with Sommelsdijk, Dirksland, Melissant, Roxenisse and 't Somerlant.

name: Ängelholm
Settlement_Description: In 1516 king Christian II (1513-1523) founded the town of Ängelholm by the river of Rönne Å.
Town_Description: In 1516 king Christian II (1513-1523) granted town privileges to the newly established Ängelholm. At the same time the king ordered the inhabitants of the nearby towns of Luntertun, which was located further downstream Rönne Å, to move to Ängelholm. In 1547 Ängelholm lost its town privileges, and the inhabitants were ordered to move to Landskrona. At least some citizens decided to stay in Ängelholm.
Fair_Description: In 1516 king Christian II (1513-1523) relocated the annual fair previously held in Grevie to Ängelholm. In 1540 only two annual fairs were allowed in Scania, one in Lund and one in Ängelholm. The date and character of the fair is unknown.
Harbour_Description: Access to the sea via the river of Rönne Å. A harbour was established at the river bank. The character of the medieval harbour is, however, uncertain.

name: Campen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 976. The settlement disappeared when the island of Noord-Beveland was flooded in 1530. After the land reclamation of the Heer Janszpolder in 1699, the settlement Kamperland was built at the site of the old Campen.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The existence of a ferry between Veere and Campen is attested by the old name of Veere, Campvere, first mentioned in 1282. In 1521, the place of departure in Campen was located "ten gasthuyse" (at the hospital), probably a piece of land owned by the hospital of Middelburg. Its precise location is nevertheless unknown, due to the island of Noord-Beveland being flooded in 1530 and only reclaimed in the 17th century.

name: Ouwerkerk
Settlement_Description: The "old church" in Duiveland, discerning it from the nearby "new church" (Nieuwerkerk) is first mentioned in 1233. It was dedicated to St Gertrude.

name: Tommarp
Fair_Description: At a common meeting in 1504 the towns of Scania decided only to allow a limited number of annual fairs in the province. One of these legal annual fairs of Scania was located in Tommarp.

name: Strype
Ferry_Description: A ferry to Goedereede departed from Strype, which was probably located just north of Rockanje, at the former mouth of the creek with the same name. From 1595, the ferry also sailed to De Quack and Hellevoetsluis.

name: Falkenberg
Settlement_Description: Near the outlet of the river of Ätrans the royal castle of Falkenberg was built in the 13th century. A settlement with the same name as the castle soon developed around the castle.
Town_Description: During the 14th century the settlement near the castle had an urban character. Apparently another urban settlement developed nearby as several written sources from the 15th century mentions both Ny Falkenberg (New Falkenberg) and Gammel Falkenberg (Old Falkenberg). During the 15th century mayors, citizens, town councils and town bailiffs were mentioned in either both or one of the two towns. In 1522 Christian II (1513-1523) ordered the citizens of Old Falkenberg to move to the new town. In 1578 the town lost its town privileges for a certain period of time.

name: Simrishamn
Settlement_Description: Originally a fishing village and probably also harbour for the neighboring inland town of Tommarp. In 1161 king Valdemar the Great donated the parish church in Simrishamn to the monastery in Tommarp.
Town_Description: Probably a privileged town around 1300. Citizens and the town of Simrishamn were first mentioned in 1329. Mayors and a town council documented in 1408, but these civic institutions were probably introduced in the 14th century. Strong German economic interests in the town during the 14th and 15th centuries; a German guild was probably founded in the 14th century. Throughout the late medieval period and into the early modern era the town benefited from the rich fishing of herring in the Baltic Sea.
Fair_Description: In the 14th century Simrishamn became one of the annual fairs in Scania. Like the other international annual fairs in Scania the fishing market in Simrishamn probably took place from August 15th to October 9th, and as the other Scania fairs, the one in Simrishamn lost its importance during the 16th century.

name: Griethausen
Fair_Description: Two fairs are found in 1373: 1) Sunday after Pentecost, 2) Sunday after Sept. 17, both 2 days before and after. A weekly market took place on Tuesday-Thursday.
Toll_Description: A land toll of the Count of Cleves in Griethausen is mentioned in 1319. In 1356, the river toll of Nijmegen was moved to Griethausen as well, in 1385-1400 it was temporarily levied in Beek, and from 1419/20 in Büderich. In 1405, the tariff was ca. 2 1/2 florin.

name: Zwartewaal
Ferry_Description: A ferry to Den Briel is first mentioned in 1332.

name: null
Toll_Description: 1) The Count of Cleves levied a Rhine toll here between 1288-1472, 1485-1495 and from 1500 a river toll on the Rhine was levied. Tolls were mainly levied on wine, so a tariff of 2 shillings per barrel applied in 1290. For more information on tariffs and revenues, see source. This toll was probably established as the successor to the Orsoy toll. From 1352, Duisburg customs were also levied in Büderich. From about 1438 onwards, customs tariffs were differentiated according to whether the goods took the Rhine or the Waal route. 2) During the Soest feud (1444-1450), a fee for save conduct on the river was also levied. This is documented in 1445, but was not continued thereafter.

name: Nauerbro
Bridge_Description: Originally a ford across a small river (Ringsted Å) at the main route between Ringsted and Holbæk. Around 1585 a wooden bridge was constructed near Ejlstrup. In 1605, however, the bridge was destroyed during a flood. It was not rebuilt before 1639.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The old harbour of Zierikzee originated around a dam in a creek that was built around 1000. It was originally connected to the Gouwe in the east, but when it started to silt up, a new harbour canal was built southwest towards the Oosterschelde in 1597-1599.

name: Beldert
Settlement_Description: Settlement around the harbour of Dreischor, first mentioned in 1470-1471.
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Dreischor (at that time a separate island) is first mentioned in 1343/44. In 1361/62, Zierikzee and Duiveland are mentioned as destinations. From 1470/71, Beldert (Bellaerde) is mentioned as the departure point for the ferry to Zierikzee.

name: Dreischor
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1206. The name refers to the village as well as a separate island, that was connected to the island Schouwen in 1401.

name: Bommenede
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1165 as an island. The settlement was sometimes referred to as town, but did not possess town rights. It was an important Holland fortress in the 16th century, but drowned in 1682 and was never rebuilt.
Fair_Description: In 1557 (nov.) geeft koning Filips II een week- en een jaarmarkt. Bommenede in het Land van Voorne is te dichtbevolkt om de eigen bevolking te voeden. Veel visschepen uit diverse steden komen hier om te bevoorraden. De weekmarkt was vergaan door diverse inundaties maar de haven is nu beschermd door twee hoofden. De jaarmarkt is op 6 juli t/m de 13e, de weekmarkt op donderdag. De ingezetenen van Bommenede zijn verplicht hun koren eerst op de eigen markt te brengen voor het elders te voeren en hun koren op de eigen molen te laten malen.
Ferry_Description: A ferry between Bommenede and Hellevoetsluis existed since 1595, when it was leased to Cornelis Lievensz. for 10 years. A ferry also sailed in the other direction.
Harbour_Description: In 1557 the harbour is protected by two jetties. Around 1562 there were 30 ships for the cathc of salted fish.

name: Stolwijk
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in 1330, but might be much older, as the area was cultivated before 1200.
Fair_Description: A horsefair (Martini Translatie: July 4) and a fair for horned cattle (eve before St. Luke: October 17) each for two weeks in Stolwijk, centrally located in the Krimpenerwaard, were relocated in 1412 (June 27) towards Schoonhoven by the count of Holland. No other information is preserved for the fairs in Stolwijk.

name: Hoogvliet
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Oedenvliet (used as placename up to the 16-th century) is first mentioned in 1383.

name: Hekelingen
Ferry_Description: A ferry from Hekelingen to Moerdijk is first mentioned in 1379.

name: 's-Gravenambacht
Settlement_Description: Place-name does not exist anymore now a days.
Ferry_Description: A ferry in 's-Gravenambacht is first mentioned in 1379.

name: Dirksland
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1284. Toll-exemption was received from the count of Holland in 1421.
Fair_Description: Emperor Charles V granted in Juli 1544 a weekly market on Wednesday and a free (horse-)fair on four days in June.

name: null
Ferry_Description: There was an important Saale crossing in Alsleben since the Early Middle Ages, which was only replaced by a bridge in 1867.

name: Sommelsdijk
Fair_Description: In 1486 (24 aug.) staan Maximiliaan roomskoning en Filips aartshertog na advies van de rentmeester Beoosterschelde en van de Grote Raad aan de heer en vrouw van Ravenstein in de parochie en dorp Sommelsdijk een week- en jaarmarkt toe. In 1487 (11 okt.) ordonneert de vrouwe van Sommelsdijk dat binnen land en heerlijkheid voortaan een weekmarkt op maandag en een jaarmarkt gehouden zal worden op St. Bartholomeus (24 aug.).

name: null
Ferry_Description: Ferry connections existed between Oudenhoorn and Sommelsdijk (possibly in one direction only). The Oudenhoorn ferry was relocated to Hellevoetsluis between 1594 and 1596.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Eendracht in Tholen is first mentioned in an account of the lord of Tholen and Schakerloo in 1343. It was leased eternally to the town of Tholen in 1462. It sailed to Halsteren, and from ca. 1550 to the 's-Heer Boudewijnspolder. After the inundation of the polder in 1583, ferry services must have stopped temporarily. In 1684, the ferry was again put into service.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry across the Eendracht to Tholen sailed from ca. 1550 to the new 's-Heer Boudewijnspolder. After the inundation of the polder in 1583, the ferry services were temporarily stopped. In 1684 they were started again, to the dunes near Halsteren.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry across the Eendracht to Tholen, first mentioned in 1343, sailed to Halsteren, from ca. 1550 to 1583 to the 's-Heer Boudewijnspolder. In 1684 the ferry sailed to the dunes near Halsteren again.

name: Stavenisse
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1206. The village was located on an island of the same name, that was flooded in 1509 and reclaimed in 1599.

name: Nieuw-Vossemeer
Settlement_Description: The village Nieuw-Vossemeer was founded in 1567 when the surrounding polder of the same name was reclaimed from the sea.

name: Heffen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in c. 1188, in a copy from c. 1243.

name: Sluizen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1139. Named after a lock in the Jeker river.

name: Duingen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned between 826 and 876. The borough ('flecken') was an important site of pottery production with supra-regional importance.

name: Coppengrave
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1400 as administrator's farm ('meierhof'). Moved to the current location in the first half of the 15th century. The village was an important centre for the production of ceramics with supra-regional importance.

name: Voorschoten
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 918-948, in a copy from the 11th century.
Fair_Description: The fair must have existed in the first half of the 13th century. The village was situated on the old landroute along the coast of Holland, used by merchants from Flanders on their way to Friesland. Circa1300 the lord of Wassenaer had as burgrave here the market and its tolls, and during the fair the ell, butter-measure and the weigh-house. He also was proprietor of the cloth-hall. The accounts of the steward of the lord of Wassenaer preserved since 1554 with gaps mention a fair with  St. Peters-eve ad vincula (day before August 1). A manual of the toll-keeper of Geervliet dated 1562 mentions the horse-fair in Voorschoten on July 29 in a calendar of many horse-faires.

name: Rockanje
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 1220.

name: Staalduinen
Toll_Description: In 1454 known ('Andunen') as an outpost of the toll of the count of Holland at Geervliet.
Ferry_Description: In 1378 a ferry to Brielle is known.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Aa in Aldrup is mentioned in 1616 and was maintained by the settlement ('bauerschaft').

name: Hedikhuizen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 997, in a 13th-century copy.

name: Saerbeck
Settlement_Description: The parish village is first mentioned in the eleventh century.

name: Hanssum
Toll_Description: A river toll on the Maas as a fief of the Lord of Horn and Altena is attested in 1345 ('Haenschem'). In 1394 Roermond bought off this toll in 'Haempsem'. In 1465 the toll is a fief held by the town from the count of Horn. In 1555 the toll-collector at Asselt collects the town tolls of Hampssen and halff the toll of Kessel. Roermond states then that the tolls were not granted by the emperor but for centuries have been property with another descent. In 1579 the oldest preserved city-account of Roermond also states that all the toll of 'Hantzem' and half the toll of Kessel belonged to the city.

name: null
Lock_Description: A lock between the Vlist and Hollandse IJssel existed in 1444, when it was destroyed by Dordrecht because it allowed circumnavigation of the Dordrecht staple. It was reconstructed later, but could only be passed by small vessels.

name: Goejanverwelle
Lock_Description: The Goejanverwelle lock is mentioned in 1544 as a flash lock that could be opened at low tide to let ships pass. It might go back to shortly after 1370, when the Dubbele Wiericke was constructed between the Hollandse IJssel and the Oude Rijn. Schoonhoven and Gouda got into a conflict about the lock in the 16th century, because it allowed the circumvention of the shipping toll in Gouda. Although Schoonhoven won (in 1569 the lock is mentioned as a full pound lock), the connection remained of local importance only.

name: Empe
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1046, in a copy from the 12th century.

name: Putten
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 855, in a copy from ca. 900.
Toll_Description: In 1454 known as an outpost of the toll of the count of Holland at Geerviet.

name: Mönchpfiffel
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 830-850 in the tithe register of the monastery Hersfeld.

name: Ulft
Settlement_Description: A castle on the confluence of the IJssel and Aa rivers was first mentioned in 1122. In the 16th century, a village developed on the opposite side of the IJssel.
Toll_Description: A land toll of the Lord of Bergh is mentioned in 1475.

name: Wurzbach
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in 1250. It became a town in 1930.

name: Engelanderholt
Settlement_Description: Engelanderholt is the name of a forest, but also of an elevated clearing in the woods where justice was administered and meetings took place. The first written indications for jurisdiction at Engelanderholt date from the thirteenth century (the earliest mention of a judge in Engelanderholt dates from 1227), but the place had probably been in use before.

name: Terlet
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 1423, when Reinoud IV, duke of Guelders died here. A cross was placed in his memory, which is still mentioned on the map of the Veluwe by Christiaan Sgrooten (1573, drawn ca. 1559). At Terlet, multiple roads crossed. On the map of Elshof of 1722, two farms are mentioned: Klein Terlet (Small Terlet) and Groot Terlet (Large Terlet). The former has served as an inn at some moment in time. In 1679, Dr Niklas Nobel, syndic of Bremen, had his lunch 'zur Lüthe' between Arnhem and Deventer, which may refer to an inn at Terlet. The map of Sgrooten suggests at least one farm in the sixteenth century.

name: De Lindeboom
Settlement_Description: The inn 'De Lindeboom' is first mentioned in 1621 and was located along a Hesseroad.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry between Ammerstol and Groot-Ammers crossing the river Lek is first mentioned in 1357.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry to Schoonhoven crossing the river Lek is first mentioned in 1356. Here started the route to Gorinchem through the Alblasserwaard.

name: Gleede
Toll_Description: Toll station belonging to the count of Holland on a small isle, subordinated to the toll of Geervliet and likely replacing the toll at Strienemonde which was lost by the Elisabethfloods of 1421 and 1424. From 1470 onwards the toll was usually collected in Dordrecht at the Riedijk. Accounts are preserved and edited for the years 1531/2 and 1533/4. Outposts are then found in Puttershoek and Strijen.

name: Hengelo (Gelderland)
Settlement_Description: Earliest mention in 965, in a copy from the eleventh-twelfth century.

name: Grevie
Fair_Description: At a common meeting in 1504 the towns of Scania decided only to allow a limited number of annual fairs in the province. One of these legal annual fairs of Scania was located in Grevie. In 1516, however, king Christian II (1513-1523) relocated the fair to the newly founded town of Ängelholm. The date, age and character of the fair are unknown.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Dalem is first attested in 1417, in 1504 the destination is Woudrichem.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry over the Vennep from Hillegom to Burggravenveen is first mentioned in 1370. It was part of the road between Hillegom and Aalsmeer, that disappeared in floods probably in 1477.

name: null
Harbour_Description: In 1397 Haastrecht obtained toll-exemption from duke Albrecht of Holland and again in 1406 by his son count Willem VI. Shipping is named as means of existence in the Enqueste of 1494 as well as in the Informacie of 1514.

name: Visbrug
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Oude Rijn known as Visbrug (Fish bridge) is first mentioned in 1204, making it the oldest bridge in Leiden, together with its extension, the Sint Jansbrug. From 1427 at the latest it was built from stone. In 1532 it was widened to function as a market square.

name: null
Lock_Description: A dam with locks was built in the Vecht at Vreeland by the bishop of Utrecht in 1326. It replaced the Otterspoor dam between Breukelen and Maarssen. In 1437, the dam at Vreeland was replaced by the Hinderdam on the border between Utrecht and Holland.

name: Cartils
Settlement_Description: First mentioned after 1192. In 1257 the former countess of Cleves gave her tithe in Cartils ('Curthils') to the abbey of Rolduc ('Kloosterrade') for an annual remembrance service for her late husband, their son and herself.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Gouda is first mentioned in 1356. The destination is not given, but must have been Stolwijkersluis at the opposite bank of the river Hollandse IJssel, where the land route through the Krimpenerwaard to Schoonhoven started. Revenues for the pawning of the ferry are edited for the second half of the 14th century and early 15th century.

name: null
Toll_Description: In 1454 ('Spykenesse') known as an outpost of the toll of the count of Holland at Geervliet.
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Spijkenisse is first mentioned in 1389.

name: null
Toll_Description: In 1503 a Habsburg/Guelders toll was levied on the IJssel near Hattem with silent consent from the stadtholder and council of Holland after they had forbidden the export of goods from the Oversticht to Gelre, Weesp or Muiden. The toll was still levied in 1509, despite attempts from Deventer and the bishop to cancell the toll.For about two years (1507-1509), on the river IJssel a toll for sailing transport was levied by Burgundian soldiers stationed in Hattem, as no soldiers' pay was paid to them.

name: Schipbrug
Bridge_Description: A pontoon bridge was built around 1600. It was demolished after the construction of the new Wilhelminabrug in 1948.

name: null
Harbour_Description: A second harbour crane is displayed on the town map of Blaeu (1652) near the Raambrug at the mouth of the Schipbeek in the IJssel.

name: Strijen
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1167, in a copy from the 14th century.
Toll_Description: In 1454 known ('Stermonde') as an outpost of the toll of the count of Holland at Geervliet.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge crossing the river Geul near 'Courtilles' (Cartils) is mentioned in an investigation of the rights of the duke of Limburg, dated 1389-93. Exact location uncertain.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The age and character of the ferry between the peninsula of Sundeved and the town of Sønderborg on the island of Als is uncertain. The ferry is mentioned in 1518, but is certainly older. Presumably, the ferry across the narrow strait between Als and Sundeved was established in the 13th century. In the late medieval period and early modern era the steward of Sønderborg Castle was responsible for the ferry.
Harbour_Description: Originally a natural harbour. Later a wharf was built, and around 1500 a royal shipyard. The harbour was frequently used by German ships, in 1399, for example, from Lübeck.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the river, Kolding Å, south of the town. The bridge was mentioned in several sources during the 16th century, but is probably significantly older. Presumably, a bridge was built in either the 13th or 14th century. Periodically, the fee collected at the bridge was an important income to the town of Kolding, who also was responsible for maintaining the bridge. In other periods the responsibility for the bridge was given to other agents. In 1609, for example, king Christian IV (1596-1648) rganted the bridge to the nobleman Eske Brock.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge crossing the river Geul near the Selzerbeek in 'Torteye' (Partij) is found in an investigation of the rights of the duke of Limburg from 1389-93.

name: Asmild kloster
Settlement_Description: The Augustin nunnery of Asmild was first mentioned in 1169. Was taken over by the king at the time of the Danish Reformation in the 1530ties.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The central motive of the oldest known town seal of Hobro is a bridge. The motive is probably a reflection of a bridge across Mariager Fjord or the river of Onsild Å.

name: Prambro (Nakskov)
Toll_Description: A bridge toll ('bropenge') was levied to fund the maintenance of the bridge.
Bridge_Description: The road from Nakskov to the south required the crossing of multiple fords around the islet Svinholm. South of Svinholm, a primitive bridge was built, which is first mentioned in 1540 when burgomaster Laurids Ulf from Nakskov acquired the right to levy the bridge toll ('bropenge') for his lifetime.

name: Sundby Færge
Ferry_Description: The age and character of the ferry across the most narrow part of Roskilde fjord is uncertain. Documented in 1516 but probably significantly older. In the 16th century two ferrymen were granted the ferry rights: one lived in Hornsherred on the western side of the shore and one near the settlement of Ude Sundby on the eastern shore. When king Frederick II (1559-1588) began building the castle of Frederiksborg in Hillerød the ferry was used for transporting building materials.

name: Neder Søgård
Settlement_Description: The village of Over Søgård was first mentioned in 1547.

name: Næsby Bro
Bridge_Description: Documented in 1612-1613 when reparations were needed, but most likely considerably older. A fee (Danish: bropenge/brokorn) was paid to cross the bridge.

name: Sundby (Lolland)
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the strait of Guldborgsund  between Nykøbing Falster and Sundby on the island of Lolland was in place by the 14th century. Presumably the ferry also existed in the 13th century.

name: Grøde
Settlement_Description: The settlement of Grøde was first mentioned in 1683, but is probably older.

name: Skibholm havn
Harbour_Description: A harbour named Skibsholm was used by the town of Slagelse, mentioned several times in the 16th century, but most likely to be older. It was probably a natural harbour at the mouth of Tudeå river. King Frederick II ordered the closure of the harbour for regular trading activities in 1574, but after complaints from citizens of Slagelse it was reopened in 1580. The harbour probably had a minor character, as only in 1650 buildings were erected on the site. After the town of Korsør became staple town in 1661, the harbour was finally closed in 1664.

name: Gedser Færge
Ferry_Description: A ferry in Gedser (or Gedesby) was apparently first mentioned in the so-called main list in King Valdemar’s Cadastre c. 1231. The ferry connected Falster with Northern Germany, probably the town of Rostock. In 1551 the people from the village of Gedesby a bit further north complained to the king over unregulated ferries in Gedser.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the strait of Guldborgsund  between Nykøbing Falster and Sundby on the island of Lolland was in place by the 14th century. Presumably the ferry also existed in the 13th century.
Harbour_Description: The harbour was used by Hanseatic merchants from the high medieval period onwards. In 1399, for example, ships from Lübeck sailed to Nykøbing Falster. A map in Resen’s Atlas Danicus from c. 1675 shows two piers.

name: Holmstrup
Fair_Description: Four annual fairs mentioned in the 16th century, but most likely to be older. In 1568 an attempt was made to relocate the fairs to Kalundborg, but apparently the market activity in Holmstrup continued. The age, date and character of the fairs is unknown.

name: Pine Mølle
Settlement_Description: A watermill is first mentioned in 1376.
Bridge_Description: It was possible to cross the river of Tudeå at the water mill by a bridge or dam. This water crossing was in 1585 described as part of the main road from Kalundborg to Korsør. It had to be maintained by the peasants from Løve shire and Slagelse shire (Danish: herred). Likely to have been two bridges at this location in the late 16th century.

name: Vindbyholt
Settlement_Description: A well documented inn from the second half of the 16th century. The inn was probably first mentioned in 1535. Visited by king Frederik II (1559-1588) and also by his son Christian IV (1596-1648).

name: Egebjerg
Settlement_Description: The village of Egebjerg was first mentioned in 1336.
Fair_Description: A fair is documented in the 16th century, but probably older. The fair was related to the fair in the nearby settlement of Vig. In 1546 the fairs of Egebjerg and Vig were relocated to Nykøbing Sjælland. The date, age and character of both fairs are uncertain

name: Vindekilde
Settlement_Description: A village mentioned for the first time around 1370. In the early 17th century two inns were found in Vindekilde.

name: Ågerup Bro
Bridge_Description: A watermill with a dam or bridge across the river of Halleby Å. The watermill is documented from around 1400.

name: Svinninge
Settlement_Description: Village first mentioned in the 14th century. The village was located near a ford across the river of Svinninge Å

name: Grønsund Færge (Falster)
Ferry_Description: The ferry across the narrow strait of Grønsund between Møn and Falster is mentioned in 1509 but is most likely to be older, presumably from the 13th century.

name: Høve
