The church of St Nicholas at the bridge head is first mentioned in 1182. After repeated destructions by floods the bridge was rebuilt in stone in 1342. Replaced by a new construction in 1976/77.

name: Schlösserbrücke
Bridge_Description: The Schlösserbrücke across the Gera is first mentioned in the 13th century as a wooden pedestrian bridge. Until 1717 the bridge and the adjoining streets were too narrow for two wagons to pass each other. A stone bridge was only built in 1736.

name: Lange Brücke
Bridge_Description: First mentioned in 1293, the long bridge was originally a single construction over two arms of the Gera river. Later it was replaced with two separate bridges. The southern entrance to the bridge was formed by the bridge head church St Vitus.

name: Roßbrücke
Bridge_Description: The Roßbrücke ('horse bridge') is one of the oldest bridges in Erfurt, and connected the Mainzer Hof with the Löbertor gate. It is unclear which character it had. A bridge with two arches is attested in 1675. The current construction is thought to date from c. 1750.

name: Löberbrücke
Bridge_Description: The Löberbrücke was built as part of the defensive system around the old town in the 14th century. It was demolished when the city moat was filled after 1900.

name: Augustbrücke
Bridge_Description: The Augustbrücke was built as part of the defensive system around the old town in the 14th century. It was demolished when the city moat was filled after 1900.

name: Krämpferbrücke
Bridge_Description: The Krämpferbrücke was built as part of the defensive system around the old town before the Krämpfertor gate, which is first mentioned in 1196. It was demolished after the city moat was filled after 1900.

name: Johannesbrücke
Bridge_Description: The bridge before the inner gate of St John was probably built in 1444. It was demolished after 1900.

name: Löbertorbrücke
Bridge_Description: The bridge before the Löbertor gate was constructed as part of the second fortification of the city after 1373. Replaced by new bridges in 1892, 1930 and 2004.

name: Schmidtstedtertorbrücke
Bridge_Description: The bridge before the Schmidtstedt gate was built as part of the second fortification of the city after 1373. Replaced by a new bridge in 1895.

name: Krämpfertorbrücke
Bridge_Description: The bridge before the outer Krämpfertor gate was built after 1373 as part of the second fortification of the city. A new bridge was built in 1895.

name: Johannestorbrücke
Bridge_Description: The bridge before the outer Johannistor gate was built after 1373 as part of the second fortification of the city. Replaced by new bridges in 1896 and 1969/71.

name: Maasdam
Toll_Description: A comital toll was found once in 1331, shortly after the count granted the lord of Altena to built a new sluice in the dam there in 1322. The dam was probably built around 1270. In 1421 the region was largely flooded with the St. Elisabeths flood but the village remained.

name: null
Bridge_Description: At the latest an the end of the 11th century, a bridge spanned the Werra at Meiningen.

name: Mehlis
Settlement_Description: First mention as part of the name Günther de Mels in 1210, but probably much older. The economy of the settlement depended on iron industry, a hammer mill is first mentioned in 1440. Acquisition of town rights in 1894. Merged with nearby Zella to the double town Zella-Mehlis in 1919.

name: Zella
Settlement_Description: The hermitage ('cella') of St Blasius was founded in 1111/12. Later the economy of the settlement depended on the iron industry and it became a market borough ('Marktflecken') in 1645. Merged with nearby Mehlis into the double town Zella-Mehlis in 1919.
Fair_Description: Four fairs were organised annually in Zella since 1645.

name: Finkenburg
Toll_Description: The water toll on the Weser river of Thedinghausen, first attested in 1260, was levied at the toll station in Eißel. Due to changes in the course of the river, the toll was moved to Intschede around 1611. The location of the toll house later became known as the farm Finkenburg.

name: Barrien
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as part of the name Albero de Beringen in 1218. The village itself is first mentioned around 1250.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge in Wahrenbrück is mentioned in a charter in 1307.

name: Mühltroff
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1242. A German settlement existed since the second half of the 12th century. A moated castle was expanded in the 13th century.
Town_Description: Acquisition of town privileges between 1350 and 1360. Mentioned as town ('Stadt') in 1367 and as borough ('oppidum') in 1378.

name: Elsterberg
Settlement_Description: Probably founded as a German border settlement against the Slavs around 1150. A knight Rayer of Elsterburg is first mentioned in 1198. The lords of Lobdeburg constructed a castle and church around 1200, first mentioned in 1225.
Town_Description: First mentioned as "civitas" in 1354. The oldest town statutes date from 1368. The town had the Magdeburg town law.

name: Schinveld
Toll_Description: Safe conduct for traffic over land was levied here in 1396 by the count of Brabant and Limburg. Possibly place for the horse-toll installed in 1389. In 1452 the toll on horses was leased with the toll of Rode, from 1533/4 onwards (possibly 1527) with the great toll of Valkenburg.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Geeste river is mentioned around 1275. On a drawing of Lehe from 1603, a ferry house is shown. A bridge was built in 1751.
Harbour_Description: On a drawing of Lehe from 1603, a small ship landing place at the Geeste river is visible, as well as a market cross. This leads to the assumption, that the place had some importance as a shore market and harbour in the Middle Ages.

name: Saalebrücke
Bridge_Description: A wooden bridge across the Saale was built at the location of a ford around 1254, based on dendrochronological evidence. Around 1300, a new wooden bridge was constructed north of it and strengthened around 1320. A bridge chapel dedicated to St Nicholas was built in 1371. The bridge lost its significance after the Saale moved its course to the East in the mid-14th century and a new stone bridge was constructed at the position of the modern Camsdorfer Brücke.

name: Lachebrücke
Bridge_Description: The canal Lache between the old town and the Saale river was constructed around 1353-1355. It was crossed by a wooden bridge that is first mentioned when it was renewed in 1532. It was rebuilt in stone before 1639 and destroyed when the Lache was filled up in 1938.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Meuse in Dinant is first mentioned in 824.

name: Villance
Fair_Description: Philip II granted a weekly market and five fairs in 1583/4 in order to restore war-damage.

name: Hénin-Liétard
Fair_Description: In 1566 king Philip II granted a fair on Monday after Exaltatio Crucis (Sept. 14).

name: Houffalize
Fair_Description: In 1528 emperor Charles confirmed the two free fairs which were granted by the counts and dukes of Luxembourg to the seigniory of Houffalize of squire Richard de Mérode and were confirmed by the king of Bohemia in 1338.

name: Torhout
Fair_Description: Around 1200 it was part together with Bruges, Ieper (Ypres), Rijsel (Lille) and Mesen (Messines) of the famous Flemish cycle of fairs who took over the one previous found in the Champagne-region. In the 13th century the fair in Torhout lasted from June 24 till July 24. In 1219 (May 13) the pope granted the church of St. Peter in Torhout the revenues from the fairs and 'kermesse'. Tariff from the market-toll for the Hansa granted in 1252 (May) by countess Margareth and a general one dated around 1270 are edited.

name: Kortrijk
Settlement_Description: Archaeological finds have shown a Roman settlement on both shores of the river Leie from the 1st to 3rd century AD. A new settlement developed directly south of it from the 4th-5th century. A fortification possibly goes back to a Viking camp in 880 and was later acquired by the counts of Flanders. The parish church of St Martin is first mentioned in 1027.
Town_Description: Town privileges were confirmed by Philipp of the Alsace, count of Flanders in 1190. The original privileges were possibly granted in 1127.
Fair_Description: A weekly market already existed around 960 and was granted by count Boudewijn. In 1251 a fair existed. In 1303 (Oct. 21) the son of the count of Flanders granted a fair starting Sept. 1 for the whole month. In 1325 fairs are found 8 days before and 14 days after Pentecost. In 1391 a fair with Eastern existed and since 1365 there were two 'oogstforen' (fairs with in harvesttime): 1) Aug. 10 for cattle and horses, 2) Aug. 26 during three days a general fair. In 1534 emperor Charles confirmed a fair with Eastern. In 1569 a flaxfair is founded.

name: Nieuwpoort (Vlaanderen)
Town_Description: Nieuwpoort was founded as town in 1163 by count Philip I of Flanders near the mouth of the river Yser in the North Sea. It received the same town privileges as Diksmuide. It functioned as the harbour for the towns of Ypres and Diksmuide.
Fair_Description: In 1163 a market-toll is found. Count Lodewijk granted a free fair in 1363 (May 30) on St. Michelsday (Sept. 29) and the following two days. Archduke Maximiliaan granted in 1495 (Jan.) a free fair after  processionday, on the Sunday after St. Jan-Baptista (June 24), and during 7 days. Guicciardini mentions in 1612 a fair in September.

name: Deinze
Fair_Description: In 1517 (May) king Charles granted a free fair on Monday after Low Sunday for three days. In 1554 a flaxfair is founded.

name: Poperinge
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in a charter of Charles the Fat as property of the abbey of Saint-Omer in 877, but the name indicates an origin in the 5th century.
Town_Description: Thierry of Alsace, count of Flanders, granted town privileges in 1147. His son Philipp granted market privileges and the right to build a canal.
Fair_Description: In 1187 marketrights were obtained. In 1272 (Jan.) the count of Flanders confirmed the right to organise a fair granted by the count of Alsace to the abbey of St. Bertin in Pouperinghe. Emperor Charles granted in 1528 a free fair during 3 days on Tuesday after the Sunday called Quasimodo (first Sunday after Eastern) and a free weekly market on Friday to restore damage caused by pestilence and fire.
Harbour_Description: Although a privilege to build a canal was already granted in 1187, a canal was only dug from 1367. This so-called Poperingevaart connected Poperinge with the Yser river.

name: Leuze-en-Hainaut
Fair_Description: In 1539 emperor Charles granted a free fair.

name: Lessines
Fair_Description: In 1275 Lessines, situated on the river Dender, had a fair with St. Matthew (Sept. 21), a market, a grain- and clothhall, wine-cellars and stone-pits. In 1565 a fair held Sunday before St. Matthew, donated by duke Philip the Good in 1453 (Sept.) was confirmed by king Philip II.

name: Geraardsbergen
Town_Description: Baldwin IV, count of Flanders, bought land around the Dender river from lord Gerald of Hunnegem in 1067-1070 and founded the town Geraardsbergen there. A small trade settlement possibly already existed before. The Benedictine abbey of St Peter, later of St Adrian, was moved from Dikkelvenne to Geraardsbergen in 1081.
Fair_Description: In 1518 (July) king Charles granted a fair on the first workingday after St. Bartholomeus (August 24) with freedom three days before and after that date. In 1565 a flaxfair is founded.

name: Perwez
Fair_Description: In 1511 (August 20) a free fair was granted by the emperor Maximilian and archduke Charles on St. Remy/Remigius (Oct. 1) for three days.

name: Rupelmonde
Fair_Description: Philip duke of Burgundy stated in 1425 on request of the inhabitants of Rupelmonde that the date of one of the two free fairs should be on the Sunday before Maria Ascension (August 15). The date of the other fair remained on the Sunday after 'Sint-Denijsdag' (Dionysius: Oct. 9).

name: Lobberich
Fair_Description: The duke of Gelre granted the parish Lobberich in the Land of Kriekenbeek in 1496 (July 20) three free fairs. In 1505 (Sept. 12) another(?)  two free fairs. NAZIEN voor data: Nijhoff VI 182 en 506

name: Rekem
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1143. Rekem was an independent lordship.

name: null
Toll_Description: The oldest source for this toll is a tariff for the tolls on the rivers Schelde and Scarpe between Douai and Rupelmonde dated 1271 and granted by countess Margareth. Rupelmonde is then the 21st watertoll downstream from Douai. The yields of the toll for the period 1379-1541 are collected. Accounts (rotuli) are preserved for the period 1250-'70(?) and 1363-1394. The toll-account dated 1385 is edited.

name: Lille
Fair_Description: A fair is known in 1127. Around 1200 it was part together with Bruges, Torhout (Thourout), Ieper (Ypres) and Mesen (Messines) of the Flemish cycle of fairs who took over the one previous found in the Champagne-region. In the 13th century the fair in Lille lasted from August 15 till Sept. 14. In 1271 a horse-fair was granted, independent of the said cycle of five Flemish fairs.

name: Mesen
Fair_Description: A fair is known around 1071-1093 when yields are given to the abbey. In 1159 the count of Flanders and his son added 4 display days (dies dedicationis) to the fair, which  started after that and lasted 15 days. Around 1200 it was part together with Bruges, Torhout (Thourout), Rijsel (Lille) and Ieper (Ypres) of the famous Flemish cycle of fairs who took over the one previous found in the Champagne-region. In 1228 a conflict between the merchants of Flanders and the abbess of Mesen was settled and the fair started with St. Remigius (Oct. 1) during 19 days. Merchants had to pay a fee called 'dorpinghe or pertusage'. Those from Bruges, Ypres, Ghent, Veurne, Dixmuide, Aardenburg, Oostburg, Oudenburg, Gravelines and Oudenaarde payed half this fee. In the 13th century the fair in Mesen lasted from Oct. 1 till Nov. 1.

name: Chimay
Settlement_Description: Situated on the crossing of the road Saint-Quentin-Trier wit Eau-Blanche.
Fair_Description: In 1517 (June) the emperor Maximilian and the archduke Charles granted a fair starting St. Ghislain (Gisleni) and St. Denis (Dionysius) (Oct. 9) for 15 days.

name: Sint-Niklaas
Fair_Description: In 1513 (June) the emperor and archduke Charles granted a weekly market and a fair on St. Nicolas (Dec. 6) for two days.

name: Roeselare
Fair_Description: A free fair was admitted by Philip the Good in 1439. The fair with St. Michel (Sept. 29) lasted from Monday till Wednesday. This was foremost a cloth-fair. The oldes town-account dated 1486/7 mentions a 'feast'. Eight days before that there was a horsefair. In 1539 a flaxfair is founded. In 1561/2 two new linenfairs and in 1569/70 a total of six linenfairs were organised.

name: Rumst
Toll_Description: Toll-tariffs for the toll of Rumst on the river Rupel are edited for the years around 1401, 1470 (1503) and 1572. Exempt around 1401 are: Brussels, Herentals, Leuven, Lier, Mechelen, Rupelmonde and Antwerp. In 1572:: Leuven, Brussels, Antwerp, Lier, Vilvoorde and Rupelmonde and possibly Gorcum (they had to register till further notice).

name: Denderwindeke
Fair_Description: Around 1457 duke Philip the Good granted a free fair on request of the lord of Goux and Wedregate.

name: Bailleul
Fair_Description: In 1501 the magistrate requested a free fair for cloth to restore damage of several fires during the last 20 years. A fair was granted by Philip the Handsome on Sept. 9 during 3 days and with safe-conduct for 15 days before and after that date.

name: Bouchain
Settlement_Description: End of the ninth century main place in Ostrevant between the rivers Scarpe and Schelde.
Fair_Description: Market-tolls are known between 1256-86. In 1528 Charles V granted a free fair for 3 days to restore damage by fire in 1521 caused by the French.

name: Hondschoote
Fair_Description: In 1539 (1531?) emperor Charles V granted a free fair during 3 days (Thursday till Saturday) after Pentecost and a weekly market on Monday on request of the lord of Gaesbeek and Hondschoote.

name: Chièvres
Fair_Description: In 1562 Philip II granted a fair to Condé on the Monday after the fair in  Chièvres on Monday after Quasimodo (Sunday after Eastern).
Toll_Description: In 1186 a toll on traded goods is found.

name: Arras
Fair_Description: Market-tolls are found in 1036 and in the early 12th century. Around 1494 Maximilian and Philip the Handsome granted a fair.

name: Marche-en-Famenne
Fair_Description: In 1311 (Sept. 24) the count of Luxemburg granted three fairs: 1) Wednesday afer Eastern, 2) Wednesday after Pentecost, 3) St. Remacle (Oct. 1 [sic !?: Sept. 3]). In 1568 king Philip II confirmed three fairs who were relocated to Exaltatrio Crucis (Sept. 14) and St. Lucie (Dec. 13) and to the Saturday before the Sunday Letare.

name: Veurne
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 877, in a copy from 961. A circular rampart was constructed around 890 as a defence against Vikings. The count of Flanders constructed a moated castle in the 11th century. East of it a trading settlement developed.
Town_Description: Veurne acquired a number of privileges and can be considered a town since c. 1180.
Fair_Description: In 1396 (July) duke Philip of Burgundy granted a fair.

name: Gistel
Fair_Description: In 1565 king Philip II granted the free fair on Wednesday and Thursday before St. Martini in Winter (Nov. 11) to be lengthened with four days.

name: null
Toll_Description: Accounts of the toll (rotuli) are preserved for the years 1383-'85. A tariff from the toll dated 1561 is edited.

name: Tielt
Fair_Description: Accounts of the toll (rotuli) are preserved for the years 1384-91. In 1564 a flaxfair is founded.

name: Armentières
Settlement_Description: First mentioned as property of the abbey of Saint-Vaast in Arras in 869. The settlement prospered in the 13th century because of cloth manufacturing, and once again with a revival in the first half of the 16th century.

name: Diksmuide
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1089. The settlement was located near the confluence of the Handzamevaart and the Yser. The lords of Esen built a castle here in the 12th century.
Town_Description: Town privileges were granted before 1163, because in that year Nieuwpoort received the same privileges as Diksmuide. The town flourished in the 13th and 14th centuries from the textile fabrication and dairy trade.
Toll_Description: A toll is found in the oldest account of the count of Flanders ('Gros Brief') dated 1187.

name: Dunkerque
Settlement_Description: Dunkerque possibly originated as a fishing village with a chapel of St Eloi in the 7th century.
Town_Description: Philipp of Alsace, count of Flanders, granted town privileges in 1182. The town only had a substantial economic development from the 14th century onwards, and was fortified at the beginning of the 15th century. The town was destroyed by the French in 1558 and rebuilt into a fortress in the 17th century.

name: Gravelines
Toll_Description: A toll with a tariff levied by the count in the town and in the harbour was installed in 1163 en renewed in 1269. Accounts of the excises on beer and wine dated 1384-'90 are preserved.

name: Saint-Omer
Fair_Description: In the late 12th century a market-toll is found. In 1271 the fair is instituted like in Thourout. In 1366 (Dec. 24) a new fair is granted by the countess on St. Michel (May 8) during 9 days.

name: Menen
Settlement_Description: Situated on the river Leie/Lys and on the road Bruges-Lille.
Fair_Description: A free fair was granted in 1351 (May 9) by count Louis de Male of Flanders and a weekly market on Saturday, together with privileges regarding drapery. The fair lasted 3 days and started Monday after the Octave of Trinitatis (Sunday after Pentecost). Accounts of the comital toll, sluice and bridge dated 1486-92 are preserved. In 1570 a flaxfair is founded.
Staple_Description: In 1351 (May 9) a staple for spinned wool in Flanders was relocated from Keselbergh to Menen by count Louis de Male of Flanders.

name: Halluin
Settlement_Description: Situated on the river Leie/Lys and on the road Bruges-Lille.

name: Wervik
Fair_Description: A free fair was granted in 1296 but diminished in the 14th century.

name: Comines
Toll_Description: A tariff of the toll dated 1354 (above all concering drapery) and a renewed version dated 1542 are edited and discussed.

name: Warneton
Settlement_Description: A market and meat house are known in the 12th century. After about 1300 Warneton took over the position from Comines as an outport for Ypres on the river Lys/Leie. The road from Ypres to Lille crossed the river here. In the 14th century drapery was important.

name: Oudenaarde
Fair_Description: A toll levied by the duke in 1462 on the fair in May was without yield. Guicciardini mentions in 1612 fairs in May en October.

name: Antoing
Fair_Description: King Philip II granted in 1570 a fair on Apr. 1.

name: Tournai
Settlement_Description: Situated on a crossing where the river Schelde was traversed. Here the route Boulogne-Cassel-Wervik-Bavay and the route Arras-Asse-Tongeren gathered.
Fair_Description: Market- and transit-tolls are known in 1153-'69.

name: Condé-sur-l'Escaut
Fair_Description: In 1562 Philip II granted a fair to Condé on the Monday after the fair in Chièvres on Monday after Quasimodo (Sunday after Eastern).
Toll_Description: A transit-toll dated late 13th century is known.

name: Couvin
Fair_Description: In 1258 two fairs are supposed and a market-toll is known. In 1377 three fairs and a weekly market on Wednesday are found.

name: Fosses-la-Ville
Settlement_Description: Situated on a crossing of the routes Dinant-Nivelles and Namur-Walcourt.
Fair_Description: In or shortly after 974 a fair was granted. In 1086 the pilgrimage of St. Folianus was transferred to the fairday. Toll and mint are found around 1100. In 1286 a hall was built.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Meuse was constructed between 1311 and 1328. It replaced an earlier bridge which existed from 1066 to the second half of the 13th century and which was located 200m upstream, connecting to the Rue du Vieux Pont.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on the Meuse is first found in 743.
Harbour_Description: It is assumed that a river harbour on the Meuse already existed during the reign of Childeric III (743-747). From the 11th and 12th centuries, landing places for river barges existed on both sides of the mouth of the Hoyoux river. From the 14th century, landing places on the opposite shore of the Meuse river, at Huy-Petite, are also attested.

name: Grognon
Harbour_Description: The oldest and most important landing places in Namur were located at the Grognon, a land tongue at the confluence of the Meuse and Sambre rivers, which were both navigable. Archaeological finds of harbour structures date back to the 5th century. It is possibly mentioned in 954, but for the first time explicitly in 1465.

name: Pont de Jambes
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Meuse in Namur is first mentioned in 1264.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Sambre in Namur is first mentioned in 1183.

name: Orsoy
Fair_Description: Fairs took place on St Bartholomew (August 24) for 14 days until September 6 and on Friday before Sunday Oculi until the eve of Easter. The fair of St Bartholomew was relocated in 1428 from Duisburg. In 1576 four horse fairs were granted. Only Duisburg was exempt from this market-toll. Toll on the Rhine was only levied from the skippers who didn't attend the fairs.
Toll_Description: In 1242 citizens of Kleve were freed from the toll in Orsoy, Schmitthausen, Nijmegen and Huissen. In 1288 the toll was relocated to Büderich and in 1419 back to Orsoy. In 1426 the duke of Kleve freed the citizens of Orsoy from his tolls, also the second half of the toll at Orsoy. The tolls were collected near the river Rhine. Yields for the period 1428-1500 are collected. Toll-yields on the Rhine in 1481 belonging to the duke of Kleve: Orsoy: 2200 Gulden, Lobith: 5800, Huissen: 1100, Büderich: 5200.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on the Meuse is first found in 747.
Harbour_Description: It is assumed that a river harbour on the Meuse already existed during the reign of Childeric III (743-747). In the 15th century, it is attested as being on both sides of the bridge on the right river shore.

name: null
Toll_Description: In 1271 three watertolls are known: the 'grote' (big) toll at the Spei, levied by the lord of the town Pamele at the sluice on the river Schelde, the toll levied by the abbey Ename, granted in 1154 by the lord of the town and the toll at the Spei from Goessin Hoen, later called the 'kleine' (small) toll (for 3/8 part a fief from the abbey St. Peter in Gent). A fourth toll also found in 1271 was levied on land as well as on water and belonged to the lord of Petegem, and was a fief from the count of Flanders. A toll-register dated 1413-1416 is analysed. Tariffs from the little toll dated 1271 and around 1430-50 are edited.

name: Maubeuge
Settlement_Description: Around 660 a double-convent was founded, which gave birth to the town.

name: Landrecies
Fair_Description: Early 14th century lord Guy de Châtillon granted a weekly market and a fair.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Here transshipment took place at the bridge over the Leie/Lys. Goods from the landroute Ypres-Lille were traded further aboard of ships.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Mézières was an important transshipment station in the trade with Frech wine, probably already in the 13th century. A harbour on the Meuse river is first mentioned in 1358. It was located next to the bridge Pont d'Arches.

name: Pont de Pierre
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Meuse on the south side of town is first mentioned in 1397.

name: Béthune
Fair_Description: In 1373 (June 27) Philip VI king of France granted two free fairs with la Chandeleur (Candlemas: Febr. 2) and St. Bartholomeus (August 24).

name: Oudenburg
Fair_Description: In 1275 a fair is known but must have excisted in the 12th century.

name: Binche
Fair_Description: A market-toll is first found between 1256-'86.

name: Braine-le-Comte
Staple_Description: In 1460/1 the town received the staple for linen from Hainaut, before selling this on the market of Enghien. In 1515 king Charles renewed this right with the obligation for Soignies to use this staple after the magistrate of Brain-le-Comte prohibited the staple of Ath.

name: Harelbeke
Settlement_Description: The church of St Saviour existed in the 9th century. The vita of St Bertulf mentions the destruction of the church by inhabitants of Kortrijk around 990.
Town_Description: Mentioned as town since the 12th century.
Fair_Description: In 1385 a free 'feste' was granted by Philip the Bold, duke of Flanders, starting Sept. 20 and then during 3 days and with 8 days before and after that 'feste' safe-conduct.

name: Saint-Ghislain
Fair_Description: Around 1400 a weekly market was relocated from Hornu, where it was organised since the 11th century. Later a market-hall was built.

name: Cambrai
Fair_Description: Around 900 once in the two years a fair was organised. Market-tolls date before 1270.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Main in Lichtenfels is mentioned in regulations of the safe conduct of Coburg from 1492 as the end of the safe conduct.

name: null
Bridge_Description: The bridge across the Main in Eltmann is mentioned in safe conduct regulations from Coburg from 1492 as the end of the safe conduct.

name: Cuxhaven
Settlement_Description: A harbour settlement Kuckshaven is first mentioned in 1570, when the dike at the settlement was destroyed by floods. It was merged with nearby Ritzebüttel in 1872 and with Döse in 1905, after which it was elevated to a town in 1907.
Harbour_Description: A harbour in the Ritzebüttel tidal creek Schleusenpriel developed in the 16th century and was expanded in the following centuries.

name: Kaltennordheim
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 795. The administrative district ('Amt') Kaltennordheim is first mentioned in 1334, which was governed from the castle Merlinse in the settlement. The castle is first mentioned in 1350.
Town_Description: Acquisition of town privileges from Count Georg Ernst of Henneberg on 12 October 1562, although the settlement was usually referred to as borough ('flecken') afterwards.
Fair_Description: In the town privileges of 12 October 1562 Kaltennordheim also acquired the right to hold five fairs, on Sunday after Invocavit, the third Day of Pentecost, Sunday after St Kilian, Sunday after St Michael, and Sunday before St Thomas. The Pentecost market was the most important and remains today as "Heiratsmarkt".
Toll_Description: With the town privileges of 1562 Kaltennordheim also acquired the right to levy a small toll on commodities traded on the market.

name: Ter Hunnepe
Toll_Description: A toll near Epse on the road to Deventer, situated on the border of Gelre and Overijssel. The toll was named after the 13th-century convent Ter Hunnepe, which was situated on the other site of the Schipbeek. In 1395 the toll was half belonging to the duke of Gelre and half pawned to Willem ten Colc. Half-year yields of the duke amounted to 5 guilders 31 groten and 17 guilders. Later preserved accounts dated 1552-1619. Usually farmed out by the land-steward of Zutphen. In 1551 the toll was redeemed of the count of Limburg Stirum. The toll house is found on a map dated circa 1577. Remnants of the toll house, rebuilt in 1597, were found in 2019 at the Molbergsteeg.

name: Schkölen
Settlement_Description: First mention uncertain, due to confusion with a settlement with the same name near Leipzig. A friary of the monastery Pegau was founded around 1140. A market in Schkölen is mentioned in 1158, and it was seat of a regional law court ('Landding') in 1198-1288/1291.
Town_Description: Elevation to town rank in the 15th century, possibly under the lords of Bünau, who were in possession of the settlement from 1413. First mention as town in 1425. However, it was never fortified and its economy depended mainly on agriculture.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll with a tariff levied by the count in the town and in the harbour was installed in 1163 and renewed in 1269. The oldest account (rotulus) of the 'grant tonliu' is dated 1295/6 and is edited. A fresh herring-toll is found in 1295 as is stated in the oldest account dated 1301/2.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Due to storm surges in the first half of the 11th century the river Aa was deepened and subsequent canalization created an important harbour.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry between Bergen and Vierlingsbeek across the Meuse originated around 1300.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The harbour of Altenbruch was the main supply harbour for Ritzebüttel, which was owned by Hamburg since 1394, and mentioned as such between 1568 and 1618. It was located at the sluice near Altenbruch, which was built in 1313, and could be reached better than the harbour of Ritzebüttel itself until the 17th century.

name: null
Toll_Description: A bridge toll for hemp and hops was installed in 1525.

name: null
Toll_Description: The inhabitants of the village Hedel obtained toll exemption in 1378 from duke Albrecht in Holland during the life of the lady of the village (Margriet van der Lek) and her son. This right was confirmed in 1405 during the life of the lord of the village (Otto van der Lek), his wife and his mother. The river toll in Driel was relocated to Hedel in 1444, but moved back to Driel already in 1448/'9. Exempted from the toll were Doesburg, Zutphen, Arnhem, Grave, Maasbommel, Tiel, Zaltbommel, Culemborg and Heukelum. Roermond and Veen (in the Land of Heusden?) had to pay an annual fee. Emmerich and Nijmegen paid half the toll and 'bodemtol'. In 1482 archduke Maximilian confirmed the possession of the toll by the lord ten Berge as lord of Hedel, as it was pawned by his predecessor to his ancestor. A few toll accounts of Hedel are preserved at the castle of Bergh, dated 1482/1483, 1502/1503 en 1510/1511. Only the inhabitants of Den Bosch were exempted at the time. The account of the seigniory of Hedel dated 1552/1553 states again that the toll formerly was relocated to Driel. But in 1564 the toll was back in Hedel. It was still there in 1574, although without revenues as a result of the uprising against Spain.
Ferry_Description: The earliest mention of a ferry across the Meuse in Hedel dates from 1390. At the opposite river bank, the ferry moored near Fort Crèvecoeur after this fort had been build at the end of the sixteenth century. The ferry rights belonged to the Lord of Hedel, who had it leased out by an agent (‘rentmeester’). Compared to ferries nearby, it must have been a much frequented one: in the beginning of the eighteenth century, the ferry rights of Hedel amounted to 560 guilders, whereas the pedestrian ferry Bokhoven-Hedel (which existed since 1688) came to 10 guilders only. The account of the seigniory of Hedel dated 1552/1553 mentions a ferry on the river Meuse farmed out for 111 gold guilders per year. The ferry fees differentiated between inhabitants of the barony of Hedel and ‘strangers’; the latter had to pay more. The ferry was replaced by a pontoon bridge in 1864.

name: Wiel
Settlement_Description: The settlement is first mentioned in 1347.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry is found in 1368. Later on it was held in long lease by the lord of Bokhoven and afterwards it was an emolument of the castellan of Heusden.

name: Uitgeest
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1105-1120, in a copy from c. 1420.

name: Baarland
Fair_Description: In 1580 the inhabitants of Baarland requested permission to have a horse-fair, which was granted (May 5) by stadtholder William of Orange yearly on the Wednesday after Bamis (Oct. 1).

name: null
Harbour_Description: Harbour for the river Steenwijker Aa, upon which predominantly peat was transported, which had to be transshipped in Blokzijl. The harbour fell out of use when the canal Steenwijkerdiep was constructed between 1626 and 1632, with a new harbour a bit further to the west.

name: null
Toll_Description: In 1630 the council of Steenwijk acquired permission to levy a toll on the Steenwijkerdiep, which became navigable in 1632. On St Martin's Day 1632 the toll was first rented out to Wiebrand Jochems for 1525 gold guilders. Inhabitants of Muggenbeet and Scheerwolde, who had helped with the construction of the canal, were exempted from the toll.
Harbour_Description: The canal Steenwijkerdiep was dug in 1626-1632 and enabled larger ships to export peat from Steenwijk to Holland without the need of transshipment in Blokzijl. On a map of Steenwijk by Blaeu (1949), we can see the new harbour with a simple lifting crane and a toll house.

name: Steenwijkerzijl
Toll_Description: In 1518, 1529/1530 and from 1542 onwards a toll on peat was levied in the 'groote Zyll' (Steenwijkerzijl), which was privileged by bishop Philip of Burgundy. Accounts are preserved for the years 1561-1566, combined with the toll at Kuinre, and for 1568 combined with Zwartsluis. At all three toll stations, Steenwijk was exempted.
Lock_Description: The sluice Steenwijkerzijl was already mentioned in 1375 as large sluice ('Groote zijl'), probably to discern it from the smaller Vollenhoofse Zijl. The sluice connected the Zuiderzee with the Noorderdiep and Steenwijker Aa and was constructed by Steenwijk. In 1438 the town Kampen requested to block the sluice with poles to prevent ships using it as a passage. However, it was reconstructed as a pound lock around 1550 and used for peat ships from Steenwijk with destination in Holland. The lock fell into disrepair in the 18th century and was filled in in 1794, leaving the street name Oude Verlaat as a reminder.

name: Vollenhoofsezijl
Toll_Description: The conversion of the Vollenhoofse Zijl into a pound lock led to a conflict with Steenwijk, who feared a reduction of revenues from the toll at the Steenwijkerzijl. In 1640 it was agreed that both locks would be administered together.
Lock_Description: The sluice Vollenhoofsezijl was converted into a pound lock in 1636. It fell into disrepair in the 18th century and was completely reconstructed in stone in 1707-1709. It was reconstructed in concrete slightly more to the south in 1913.

name: Arembergersluis
Lock_Description: A canal was dug between Friesland and Overijssel by stadtholder Jan de Ligne count of Aremberg in 1548-1568. It allowed vessels to avoid the open sea. It was connected with the Zwarte water in Zwartsluis with a lock. Yields of a toll levied here from peat and the number of 'lasten' peat passing the lock, both starting 1688 are edited.

name: Ossenzijl
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1437, after a sluice ('zijl').
Lock_Description: Ossenzijl is named after a sluice ('zijl'). Until 1810 it was only 4 feet wide and therefore only passable for very small vessels. The lock was removed in 1930.

name: Oude Buitenhaven
Harbour_Description: In the northern part of the old defensive canal around the city, the Burgel, there existed a harbour, which is first mentioned in 1456. Nowadays it is known as Oude Buitenhaven. The main harbour, however, was located at the IJssel riverfront around the bridge (see there).

name: null
Harbour_Description: In the fourteenth and fifteenth century, Bruneppe had a harbour with a 'lastasie', a shipbuilding yard. Probably it was only used for repairs, not for building seagoing ships. Merchants from other places had to pay 'paalgeld' in order to unload goods here.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Wageningen was originally located directly at the Nederrijn, but was of little importance as a harbour town. When the course of the river moved south in the 15th century, the town lost its connection with the river. Only in the course of the 16th century the old river bed was re-used to create a harbour canal.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A ferry between the Schlachte and the Neustadt was installed in 1645. A ferry house on the southern side was only built in 1703. For further details, see Schlachte.

name: Lage Zwaluwe
Toll_Description: Outpost of the comital toll. In 1473 with limitation: "ende dairomtrent totter vrijheit van den Berge [Geertruidenberg] toe aen die westzijde geheeten tNederveen", tariff: ox, cow or bull: ½ groot, four sheeps: 1 groot. In 1476: "ende dairomtrent streckende tot Randenrode".

name: null
Toll_Description: The bishop of Utrecht granted a toll over the bridge across the harbour in 1383, in order to maintain it. Fees were set for wagons, carts and animals. The bridge was probably not located on a thoroughgoing route and later we don't hear about the toll any more.
Bridge_Description: The bishop of Utrecht granted the levying of a toll on the bridge that was built over the harbour in 1383.

name: Spakenburg
Settlement_Description: Spakenburg is first mentioned in 1435. It developed as a fishing village at the Zuiderzee coast.

name: Lommatzsch
Settlement_Description: First mentioned before 1190. A town was founded before 1206 next to an already existing settlement, which is from then on called Altlommatzsch.
Town_Description: Foundation of a town before 1206. First mention as 'civitas' in 1286.
Fair_Description: A fair on Saturday after Letare is first mentioned in 1445. It was moved to Meißen in 1475. A second fair is mentioned in 1479.

name: Lombardsijde
Toll_Description: Toll-accounts dated 1432-1507 on the transport from English linen via the harbour of Lombardzyde to Brabant are preserved.

name: Saint-Hubert
Settlement_Description: Trading place around the abbey in the early middle-ages.
Fair_Description: The oldest proof for a fair in St. Hubert dates back to 825-837. In the 15th century there are five fairs, which decay in the 16th and 17th centuries.

name: null
Harbour_Description: A winding hole ('zwaaikom') was constructed in the Leie by the counts of Flanders in the 11th century.

name: null
Ferry_Description: The ferry across the Elbe in Arneburg is mentioned in 1424, when margrave Frederick bought back the fourth part of the ferry from Botho and Henning of Einbeck.

name: null
Ferry_Description: In 1499 the family of Kröcher was enfeoffed with the village and ferry of Räbel. In 1583 the ferrymen of Räbel had established a wagon ferry, about which they had to come to an agreement with the cathedral chapter of Havelberg, on whose lands they landed.

name: null
Ferry_Description: In 1499 the family of Kröcher was enfeoffed with the village and ferry of Räbel. In 1583 the ferrymen of Räbel had established a wagon ferry, about which they had to come to an agreement with the cathedral chapter of Havelberg, on whose lands they landed.

name: Roudnice nad Labem
Toll_Description: According to a report from merchants from Pirna in 1577, the tariffs of the toll and safe conduct in Roudnice had been tripled in eight years. Roudnice is also mentioned as toll station in the early 17th century.

name: Menistensluis
Lock_Description: The lock in the Nieuwe Vecht where it met the Nieuwe Wetering was constructed around 1600 during construction works to make the canal navigable again.

name: null
Lock_Description: A lock in the Nieuwe Vecht where it met the river Vecht was constructed around 1600 as part of construction works to renew the navigability of the canal.

name: Mělník
Toll_Description: Mentioned as toll station on the Elbe river at the beginning of the 17th century.

name: Veselí
Toll_Description: Mentioned as a toll station on the Elbe river at the beginning of the 17th century.

name: Bad Schandau
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1408. Founded as a planned town in the 15th century. It is uncertain if a fishing settlement existed before.
Town_Description: First mentioned as small town ('statichen') in 1445.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll on the Elbe river is mentioned at the beginning of the 17th century.
Ferry_Description: A ferry across the Elbe is first mentioned in 1547, but probably older.
Harbour_Description: In the 17th century, vessels from Bohemia were only allowed to sail as far as Schandau or Pirna.

name: null
Harbour_Description: The canalised Becque connected Hondschoote to the river Colme. A harbour is shown by Jacob van Deventer in the southern part of town.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Saale was built in 1602. Before that year, traffic used a ford.

name: Tochheim
Toll_Description: According to a report from 1577, a toll was levied by the count of Barby in Tochheim, which had not been levied before. After a raise in tariffs in 1612, some timber merchants on the Elbe refused to pay the toll, leading to a court case before the Imperial Chamber Court.

name: Milow
Toll_Description: A land and water toll in Milow is mentioned in 1533. Citizens of the old town Brandenburg were exempted from the water toll for their own commodities.

name: Verlaat
Toll_Description: A toll was levied at the lock of a half Brabant stuver for each ship.
Lock_Description: In 1523 bishop Philipp of Burgundy gave permission to construct a lock in the Steenwijker Aa. When the canal Steenwijker Diep was dug in 1626-1623, the lock was demolished and rebuilt 300m to the west.

name: null
Toll_Description: A toll was levied at the lock of a half Brabant stuver for each ship.
Lock_Description: Bishop Philipp of Burgundy gave permission in 1523 to build locks in the Steenwijker Aa to improve the navigability. One of them was probably located near Spijkerboor.

name: null
Harbour_Description: A new canal was dug between Ypres and the Yser river in 1637-1642, as a replacement for the narrow Ieperlee canal. A new harbour was constructed north of the old town.

name: Sas van Boezinge
Lock_Description: The engineer Bartholomeus de Buck designed a lock ('sas') near Boezinge, which replaced four separate boat hauling installations ('overdrachten') in the old Ieperlee as part of the construction of a new canal between Ypres and the Yser river. The new lock could overcome a height difference of 6.72m and was built in 1643.

name: Uedem
Fair_Description: A fair on 10 August is mentioned in 1359, with a duration of three days before and after, and a weekly market on Sunday. The weekly market took place on Tuesdays in 1431.

name: Preungesheim
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 772.

name: Eckenheim
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned in 795.

name: Eschersheim
Settlement_Description: The village is first mentioned around 1000.

name: Witte Kruis
Settlement_Description: An inn called "Witte Kruis" was located here until 1967. In the seventeenth century, it was also referred to as "Heycktegut", which referred to a nearby property.

name: Grünewalde
Settlement_Description: First mentioned in 1447. In 1639/45 a border checkpoint between Magdeburg and Saxony was installed here, where also a toll was levied on the river traffic.
Toll_Description: A toll on the river Elbe is levied here in the 17th century, which was related to the installation of a border station here in 1639/45.

name: Het Nest
Settlement_Description: Inn t'Nest is mentioned on a map dating from ca. 1690.

name: Den Engel
Settlement_Description: Den Engel is mentioned in 1639 as a farmstead and inn, named after its occupant Engel Jansen. It kept its function - later as a hotel - until the twentieth century.

name: null
Harbour_Description: Until c. 1300 Comines functioned as an outport of Ypres on the river Lys. After that year Warneton took over this position.

name: Vinkkilä (Vehmaa)
Settlement_Description:
<b>Inn:</b> Vehmaa parish constable was periodically located in Nummi, and more permanent after 1584. Parish constables (fi: nimismies, sw: länsman) were obliged to keep a tavern in late 16th c. and early 17th c. After 1650, the inn moved to Laittinen. 

<b>Post house:</b> In 1638, the Royal Steward Bernhardt Steen von Steenhousen established a post house in the village of Vinkkilä in Vehmaa.

name: haven dordrecht
Harbour_Description: Of old the waterroute called 'Thuredrecht' was the connection between the rivers Dubbel and the Meuse south and to the Merwede north. In the old harbour (Voorstraat and Wijnstraat) transshipment took place on bigger ships. Here on both sides were lots of warehouses. In 1410 the magistrate gave way for the Nieuwehaven (new harbour) by raising a sandbar in the river. After the St. Elisabeths flood of 1421 the town was almost complete surrounded by water. This hampered the development of the harbour and town. Between 1465 and 1529 the Riedijksharbour and the Hout- (wood-)harbour are constructed. Before 1565 the Bomhaven (near the Grote Kerk) by building outside the townwalls in the river some breakwaters. In 1574 the Spuiharbour was built by making a connection between the ditch and the river.A crane is first mentioned in 1273. The map of Jacob van Deventer dated 1544 shows three cranes and a wooden stockade. The map of Braun and Hogenberg dated circa 1572 has six harbour-cranes, which indicates the staple-function of the harbour.

name: Bollingerfähr
Ferry_Description: The ferry Bollingerfähr first appears in the 14th century.

name: Meyenkrebsbrücke
Bridge_Description: A bridge across the Peene north of Demmin to Meyenkrebs is attested in the 17th century. The bridge was demolished by the Swedes in 1678 and had to be rebuilt.

name: null
Ferry_Description: A bridge across the Peene near Jarmen was constructed in 1863. Before this year there existed a ferry.

name: Steinbecker Brücke
Bridge_Description: At the crossing of the Ryck north of Greifswald probably originally existed a ferry. A bridge was built here after the right of fortification from 1264. It was probably a wooden draw bridge, which is also attested in a rebuilding of 1764.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge across both branches of the Oder between Gryfino and Mescherin was built with permission of Duke Otto I in 1306. A causeway across the river island connected both wooden bridges. The bridges were destroyed by the Swedes at the end of the Thirty Years' War and not rebuilt until 1857-1860.

name: null
Bridge_Description: A bridge across both branches of the Oder between Gryfino and Mescherin was built with permission of Duke Otto I in 1306. A causeway across the river island connected both wooden bridges. The bridges were destroyed by the Swedes at the end of the Thirty Years' War and not rebuilt until 1857-1860.

name: Locht (B)
Toll_Description: Outpost of the Brabantse Landtol on the route to the fairs of Bergen (op Zoom).

name: Sannäs (Karjaa)
Settlement_Description:
<b>Inn:</b> Grabbacka tenant farm, Bältari, run an alehouse in Sannäs village (Sannainen) in 1570.

<b>Post house:</b> In 1638, the Royal Steward Bernhardt Steen von Steenhausen established a post house in the village of Sannäs in Karjaa.

name: Oinila (Paimio)
Settlement_Description: <b>Post house:</b> According to sources, a post house operated in Pertuntalo, located in the village of Oinila in Paimio, from 1640 to 1644.

name: Kulla (Tenhola)
Settlement_Description: <b>Post house:</b> In 1638, the Royal Steward Bernhardt Steen von Steenhausen established a post house in the village of Kulla in Tenhola.

name: Reitkalli (Vehkalahti)
Settlement_Description: <b>Post house:</b> In 1638, the Royal Steward Bernhardt Steen von Steenhausen established a post house in the village of Reitkalli in Vehkalahti.

name: Mynämäki
Settlement_Description: Permanent agricultural settlement in Mynämäki (sw. Virmo) goes back to the Iron Age. Ecclesiastical parish was established in the beginning of the 13th century and mentioned in 1309. Stone church was built between 1425 and 1440.
Fair_Description: The annual winter and autumn fairs of Mynämäki on Candlemas (2 February) and St Laurentius (10 August) were in 1623 moved to Uusikapunki (sw. Nystad). Mynämäki Candlemas fair was further in 1625 combined with three Lokalahti and Vehmaa area fairs into a single fair on second Sunday of Lent (15 February – 21 March) in Uusikaupunki. Mynämäki St Laurentius fair was apparently of medieval origin and was held at the fest of one of the two patrons of the parish church mentioned in 1418 (St Laurentius and St Erik). The fair site was likely somewhere close to the church next to the common road and bridge.

name: null
Toll_Description: A bridge fee was introduced in 1662.

name: Kettwig vor der Brücke
Toll_Description: The Duke of Berg levied a land toll in 1471. Tariffs and revenues are not known.

name: Haus Balken
Toll_Description: The Count of Cleves levied a land toll duty in Vynen in 1319. According to Oediger and Ilgen the toll was levied at Haus Balken on the road Xanten-Kleve. Tariffs and revenues are not known.

name: Engers
Toll_Description: A Rhine toll was levied by Dietrich von Ahrenfels, lord of Isenburg, in 1319, but it was abolished in the same year under pressure of the archbishop of Trier. From 1412 onwards the archbishop of Trier levied a Rhine toll in Engers. Tariffs are known for various years in the 15th century, see Pfeiffer.

name: null
Toll_Description: A Rhine toll was levied by the archbishop of Mainz in 1298-1302 and from 1307 onwards. Tariffs were calculated in tournois per load (fuder), with varying amounts for various years. The toll station in Oberlahnstein was one of the Rhine toll stations with the highest revenues, in the 1460s exceeding 15,000 guilder per year. For exact tariffs and revenues, see Pfeiffer.In 1333/1334 the archbishop of Mainz also levied a toll on the Lahn river.

name: Sankt Goarshausen
Toll_Description: The count of Katzenelnbogen acquired the right to levy a Rhine toll of 1 tournois per load (Zollfuder) in Sankt Goarshausen, but apparently this toll was realised in Sankt Goar on the opposite shore of the river. In 1378 the Count Palatine levied a Rhine toll of 3 tournois per Zollfuder, but this existed only temporarily. Revenues are not known.

name: Ehrenfels
Toll_Description: Imperial toll station at the Rhine, first attested in c. 1305, since 1310 owned by the archbishop of Mainz. For tariffs and revenues, see Pfeiffer.

name: null
Toll_Description: Rhine toll station, first attested in 1161/65. Originally a fief of the archbishop of Mainz, since 1198/1206 an imperial fief of the Rhinegraves. For tariffs und revenues see Pfeiffer.

name: Hövel
Settlement_Description: The village was originally called Aldenlinne and is first mentioned in 1271. The manor "tom Houele" in Aldenlinne is first mentioned in 1461, after which the entire village was renamed in the 16th century.
